title.raw: 卷一百七十四 志第一百二十七 食貨上二 Volume 174 Treatises 127: Finance and Economics 1b

sentences.zh: 食貨上二

translations.literal: Finance and Economics, Part Two
translations.idiomatic: Finance and Economics, Part Two

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking a section subtitle.
translations.idiomatic: Opening bracket for the section heading.

sentences.zh: （方田賦稅）〉

translations.literal: Closing bracket: (Square Fields and Land Tax).
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: Square Fields and Land Tax.

sentences.zh: 方田神宗患田賦不均，熙寧五年，重修定方田法，詔司農以《均稅條約並式》頒之天下。

translations.literal: As to Square Fields: Emperor Shenzong was distressed that land taxes were uneven. In the fifth year of Xining, the Square Fields law was revised and fixed anew; an edict ordered the Directorate of Agriculture to promulgate throughout the empire the 《Treatises and Formulas on Equal Taxation》.
translations.idiomatic: The Square Fields system began because Emperor Shenzong was troubled by unequal land taxes. In Xining 5 the law was revised, and the Directorate of Agriculture was ordered to issue the 《Treatises and Formulas on Equal Taxation》 empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 以東西南北各千步，當四十一頃六十六畝一百六十步，為一方；

translations.literal: Taking one thousand paces on each of the four sides—east, west, south, and north—as equal to forty-one qing, sixty-six mu, and one hundred sixty paces, this constituted one square.
translations.idiomatic: Each field square was one thousand paces on every side, equivalent to 41 qing, 66 mu, and 160 paces.

sentences.zh: 歲以九月，縣委令、佐分地計量，隨陂原平澤而定其地，因赤淤黑壚而辨其色；

translations.literal: Each year in the ninth month the county would commission the magistrate and assistant to partition the land and measure it, fixing parcels according to hills, plains, and marshes, and distinguishing them by color according to red silt, black clay, and loam.
translations.idiomatic: Every ninth month, magistrates and assistants divided and measured the land, classifying plots by terrain and marking soil types by color—red silt, black clay, loam, and the like.

sentences.zh: 方量畢，以地及色參定肥瘠而分五等，以定稅則；

translations.literal: When squaring and measuring were complete, they would jointly assess fertility and barrenness from the land and color, divide into five grades, and fix the tax rules.
translations.idiomatic: Once measurement was finished, soil was graded in five ranks from fertility and color, and tax rates were set accordingly.

sentences.zh: 至明年三月畢，揭以示民，一季無訟，即書戶帖，連莊帳付之，以為地符。

translations.literal: By the third month of the following year it would be finished; it would be posted to show the people; if for one season there was no litigation, then household placards would be written, linked with village registers and given to them as land tokens.
translations.idiomatic: Work had to be completed by the third month of the next year. Results were posted for public review; if no disputes arose within one season, household registers linked to village rolls were issued as official land certificates.

sentences.zh: 均稅之法，縣各以其租額稅數為限，舊嘗收蹙奇零，如米不及十合而收為升，絹不滿十分而收為寸之類，今不得用其數均攤增展，致溢舊額，凡越額增數皆禁。

translations.literal: The method of equalized taxation: each county took its rent quotas and tax figures as the limit. Formerly they had collected and squeezed odd fractions—for example, taking a sheng when rice did not reach ten ge, or taking a cun when silk did not reach ten fen—and now they might not use such figures to spread and extend equally, causing overflow beyond the old quota; all increases beyond the quota were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Under equalized taxation, each county was capped at its existing rent and tax totals. Officials had once rounded up odd fractions—charging a full sheng when less than ten ge of rice was due, or a full cun when silk fell short of ten fen—and such practices could no longer be used to inflate assessments beyond the old quotas.

sentences.zh: 若瘠鹵不毛，及眾所食利山林、陂塘、溝路、墳墓，皆不立稅。

translations.literal: If the land was barren saline soil that would not grow, and mountains and forests, ponds, ditches, roads, and graves that the multitude used for their benefit, on all of these no tax was established.
translations.idiomatic: Barren saline land, communal woodlands, ponds, ditches, roads, and grave sites that served public use were all exempt from tax.

sentences.zh: 凡田方之角，立土為峰，植其野之所宜木以封表之。

translations.literal: At every corner of a field square they erected an earthen mound as a peak and planted trees suited to that countryside to mark and seal it.
translations.idiomatic: At each corner of a measured square, officials raised an earthen marker and planted locally suitable trees to bound the plot.

sentences.zh: 有方帳，有莊帳，有甲帖，有戶帖；

translations.literal: There were square registers, village registers, tithing placards, and household placards.
translations.idiomatic: Records included square registers, village rolls, tithing placards, and household placards.

sentences.zh: 其分煙析產、典賣割移，官給契，縣置簿，皆以今所方之田為正。

translations.literal: For dividing households and splitting estates, mortgaging and selling, and transferring parcels, the government issued contracts and the county kept ledgers—all took as standard the land now squared.
translations.idiomatic: Household divisions, mortgages, sales, and transfers were all recorded in county ledgers and official contracts based on the newly measured fields.

sentences.zh: 令既具，乃以濟州钜野尉王曼為指教官，先自京東路行之，諸路仿焉。

translations.literal: When the orders were complete, they then appointed Wang Man, assistant magistrate of Juye in Jizhou, as instruction officer; he first carried it out in the Jingdong Circuit, and the other circuits followed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the regulations were in place, Wang Man, assistant magistrate of Juye in Jizhou, was named instruction officer and piloted the system in the Jingdong Circuit; other circuits then followed suit.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔土色分五等，疑未盡，下郡縣物其土宜，多為等以其均當，勿拘以五。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict said that dividing soil color into five grades seemed insufficient; it was sent down to prefectures and counties to assess what suited the soil, making many grades as appropriate for fairness, and not restricting to five.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, an edict held that five soil grades might not suffice; prefectures and counties were to classify land according to local conditions in as many grades as needed for fair taxation, without being limited to five.

sentences.zh: 七年，京東十七州選官四員，各主其方，分行郡縣，以三年為任。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, in the seventeen prefectures of Jingdong, four officials were selected; each took charge of his square and traveled through prefectures and counties, with a term of three years.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, four officials were chosen from Jingdong's seventeen prefectures; each oversaw assigned squares and toured the counties on three-year terms.

sentences.zh: 每方差大甲頭二人、小甲頭三人，同集方戶，令各認步畝，方田官驗地色，更勒甲頭、方戶同定。

translations.literal: For each square they assigned two senior tithing heads and three junior tithing heads; together they assembled the households of the square, ordered each to acknowledge paces and mu, the Square Fields officer inspected soil color, and again compelled the tithing heads and square households to fix it jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Each square had two senior and three junior tithing heads who assembled local households to confirm boundaries; Square Fields officers inspected soil quality, and heads and households jointly finalized the assessment.

sentences.zh: 諸路及開封府界秋田災傷三分以上縣權罷，餘候農隙。

translations.literal: In all circuits and within the Kaifeng metropolitan boundary, counties where autumn crops suffered disaster damage of three-tenths or more were temporarily suspended; the rest waited for slack season in farming.
translations.idiomatic: In all circuits and the Kaifeng metropolitan area, counties with autumn crop losses of thirty percent or more were temporarily exempted; elsewhere work waited until the farming slack season.

sentences.zh: 河北西路提舉司乞通一縣災傷不及一分勿罷。

translations.literal: The supervisory office of Hebei West Circuit requested that throughout a county, if disaster damage did not reach one-tenth, it should not be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The Hebei West Circuit supervisory office asked that counties with disaster losses under ten percent not be exempted from the program.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年，開封府言：「方田法，取稅之最不均縣先行，即一州而定五縣，歲不過兩縣，今府界十九縣，準此行之，十年乃定。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng, Kaifeng Prefecture said: Under the Square Fields law, the counties where taxation was most uneven were taken first; that is, five counties were fixed per prefecture, with no more than two counties per year. Now within the metropolitan boundary there were nineteen counties; proceeding by this rule, it would take ten years to finish.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng 5, Kaifeng Prefecture reported that under Square Fields policy the most unevenly taxed counties were to be done first—five per prefecture, no more than two per year. With nineteen counties in the metropolitan area, completion would take ten years at that pace.

sentences.zh: 請歲方五縣。

translations.literal: They requested to square five counties per year.
translations.idiomatic: It asked to measure five counties each year instead.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 其後歲稔農隙乃行，而縣多山林者或行或否。

translations.literal: Afterward it was carried out only in years of good harvest during farming slack; in counties with much mountain forest it was sometimes done and sometimes not.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the work proceeded only in good harvest years during the farming slack season, and mountainous counties sometimes participated and sometimes did not.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝知官吏擾民，詔罷之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the emperor knew that officials were harassing the people, and an edict abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, learning that officials were harassing the populace, the emperor ordered the system suspended.

sentences.zh: 天下之田已方而見於籍者，至是二百四十八萬四千三百四十有九頃雲。

translations.literal: Of fields throughout the empire that had been squared and appeared in the registers, by this time there were two million four hundred eighty-four thousand three hundred forty-nine-odd qing, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: By then, land squared and entered in the registers reportedly totaled 2,484,349 qing empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 崇寧三年，宰臣蔡京等言：「自開阡陌，使民得以田私相貿易，富者恃其有餘，厚立價以規利，貧者迫於不足，薄移稅以速售，而天下之賦調不平久矣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongning, the chief ministers Cai Jing and others said: Since opening the field paths and allowing the people to trade land privately, the rich relied on their surplus and set high prices to seek profit; the poor, pressed by insufficiency, lightly shifted tax burdens to sell quickly—and imbalance in the empire's tax levies had long persisted.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning 3, Chief Minister Cai Jing and others argued that ever since private land trade was allowed, the wealthy had inflated prices for profit while the poor had shifted tax burdens to sell quickly, leaving the empire's tax system chronically unequal.

sentences.zh: 神宗講究方田利害，作法而推行之，方為之帳，而步畝高下丈尺不可隱；

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong studied the benefits and harms of Square Fields, made the law and promoted it; squares had their registers, and paces, mu, elevation, and dimensions could not be concealed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong had studied Square Fields carefully, enacted the law, and created registers so that boundaries, acreage, elevation, and dimensions could no longer be concealed.

sentences.zh: 戶給之帖，而升合尺寸無所遺；

translations.literal: Households were given placards, and sheng, ge, and dimensions left nothing out.
translations.idiomatic: Household placards recorded dues down to the smallest measures of grain and cloth.

sentences.zh: 以賣買，則民不能容其巧；

translations.literal: For buying and selling, the people could not harbor their tricks.
translations.idiomatic: In sales and purchases, commoners could no longer hide their tricks.

sentences.zh: 以推收，則吏不能措其奸。

translations.literal: For assessment and collection, clerks could not set their frauds in place.
translations.idiomatic: In assessment and collection, clerks could no longer practice fraud.

sentences.zh: 今文籍具在，可舉而行。

translations.literal: Now the documents and registers are all in place; they can be taken up and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The records still exist and the system can be revived.

sentences.zh: 」詔諸路提舉常平官選官習熟其法，諭州縣官吏各以豐稔日推行，自京西、北兩路始。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the ever-normal granary supervisory officials of all circuits to select officers skilled in the law, instruct prefecture and county officials each to implement it in years of abundant harvest, beginning with the Jingxi and Jingbei circuits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered circuit ever-normal granary supervisors to train officials in the law and instruct prefectures and counties to implement it in good harvest years, beginning with the Jingxi and Jingbei circuits.

sentences.zh: 四年，指教官每三縣加一員，點檢官每路二員。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, one instruction officer was added for every three counties, and two inspection officers per circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, one additional instruction officer was assigned per three counties, and two inspection officers per circuit.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔諸路添置指教官不得過三員，又不專差點檢官，從提舉司於本路見任人內選差。

translations.literal: Before long, an edict said that added instruction officers in all circuits might not exceed three, and inspection officers were no longer specially assigned; the supervisory office was to select from incumbent officials within the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, an edict capped added instruction officers at three per circuit and ended dedicated inspection posts, requiring supervisors to appoint inspectors from existing circuit officials.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔罷方田。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict abolished Square Fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Square Fields was abolished by edict.

sentences.zh: 大觀二年，復詔行之，四年罷其稅賦依未方舊則輸納。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daguan, an edict again ordered it implemented; in the fourth year it was abolished, and tax levies were paid according to the old rules before squaring.
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan 2 the system was revived by edict; in Daguan 4 it was abolished again, and taxes reverted to pre-square assessment rules.

sentences.zh: 十一月，詔：「方田官吏非特妄增田稅，又兼不食之山方之，俾出芻草之直，民戶因時廢業失所。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, an edict said: Square Fields officials not only rashly increased land tax but also squared mountains that yielded no food, making people pay for fodder and grass; households abandoned their occupations and lost their places because of the season.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, an edict declared that Square Fields officials had not only inflated land taxes but also measured barren hills and charged for fodder, driving households to abandon their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 監司其悉改正，毋失其舊。」

translations.literal: Supervisory officials were to correct all of this fully and not depart from the old standards.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory officials were ordered to correct all abuses and restore former standards.

sentences.zh: 政和三年，河北西路提舉常平司奏：「所在地色極多，不下百數，及至均稅，不過十等。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe, the Hebei West Circuit ever-normal granary supervisory office memorialized: The soil colors in the locality are extremely numerous, no fewer than a hundred kinds, yet when it comes to equalized taxation there are no more than ten grades.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 3, the Hebei West ever-normal granary office reported that local soil types numbered at least a hundred, yet equalized taxation used only ten grades.

sentences.zh: 第一等雖出十分之稅，地土肥沃，尚以為輕；

translations.literal: The first grade, though paying a full ten-tenths tax, on fertile soil still was considered light.
translations.idiomatic: First-grade land paid the full rate, yet on fertile soil even that was considered too light.

sentences.zh: 第十等隻均一分，多是瘠鹵，出稅雖少，猶以為重。

translations.literal: The tenth grade was assessed only one-tenth on average; most was barren saline soil, and though the tax paid was small, it was still considered heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth-grade land was taxed at only one-tenth; much of it was barren saline soil, and though the levy was small, it was still felt as burdensome.

sentences.zh: 若不入等，則積多而至一頃，止以柴蒿之直，為錢自一百而至五百，比次十等，全不受稅；

translations.literal: If not entered in the grades, then accumulating until one reached a qing, only the value of firewood and weeds—from one hundred to five hundred cash—compared with the tenth grade, paid no tax at all.
translations.idiomatic: Land excluded from the grades could accumulate to a full qing yet be valued only at one hundred to five hundred cash for brush and weeds—less burdensome than tenth-grade land, which paid no tax at all.

sentences.zh: 既收入等，但可耕之地便有一分之稅，其間下色之地與柴蒿之地不相遠，乃一例每畝均稅一分，上輕下重。

translations.literal: Once entered in the grades, any land that could be cultivated bore a one-tenth tax; among these, inferior soil and brush land were not far apart, yet uniformly each mu was taxed one-tenth—light above and heavy below.
translations.idiomatic: Once graded, any cultivable plot owed one-tenth per mu, yet poor soil and brushland were taxed the same as better plots within the grade—making the burden lighter on the rich and heavier on the poor.

sentences.zh: 欲乞土色十等如故外，折十等之地再分上、中、下三等，折畝均數。

translations.literal: They wished to request that, besides keeping the ten soil-color grades as before, land of the tenth grade be further divided into upper, middle, and lower thirds, converting mu to equalize the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed retaining the ten soil grades but subdividing tenth-grade land into upper, middle, and lower thirds with converted acreage to equalize assessments.

sentences.zh: 謂如第十等地每十畝合折第一等一畝，即十等之上，受稅十一，不改元則；

translations.literal: That is to say, for tenth-grade land, every ten mu would convert to one mu of first grade; thus on the upper tier of the tenth grade one would bear eleven-tenths tax, without changing the original rules.
translations.idiomatic: For example, ten mu of upper tenth-grade land would convert to one mu of first-grade assessment, yielding an effective rate of eleven-tenths without altering the original tax schedule.

sentences.zh: 十等之中，數及十五畝，十等之下，數及二十畝，方比上等受一畝之稅，庶幾上下輕重皆均。

translations.literal: Within the tenth grade, when the count reached fifteen mu, and below the tenth grade when the count reached twenty mu, only then would it compare to the upper tier in bearing one mu's tax—so that light and heavy above and below might all be even.
translations.idiomatic: Middle tenth-grade land would require fifteen mu, and lower tenth-grade land twenty mu, to equal one mu of upper-tier assessment, so that burdens would be balanced across grades.

sentences.zh: 」詔諸路概行其法。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all circuits generally to implement this law.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered all circuits to adopt the reform.

sentences.zh: 五年，福建、利路茶戶山園，如鹽田例免方量均稅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, tea planters' mountain gardens in Fujian and Lizhou circuits were exempted from squaring and equalized taxation, following the precedent for salt fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, tea planters' hillside gardens in Fujian and Lizhou were exempted from measurement and equalized taxation, as with salt fields.

sentences.zh: 宣化元年，臣僚言：「方量官憚於跋履，並不躬親，行繵拍峰、驗定土色，一付之胥吏。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanhe, a court official said: The squaring officers feared traveling on foot and did not go in person; conducting rope measurement, setting peaks, and verifying soil color—they left it all to clerks.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 1, an official reported that measurement officers refused to travel the land themselves and delegated rope surveys, boundary markers, and soil inspection entirely to clerks.

sentences.zh: 致御史臺受訴，有二百餘畝方為二十畝者，有二頃九十六畝方為一十七畝者，虔之瑞金縣是也。

translations.literal: This led the censorate to receive complaints: there were cases of more than two hundred mu squared as twenty mu, and of two qing ninety-six mu squared as seventeen mu—such was Ruijin County in Qian.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate received complaints that in Ruijin County, Qianzhou, more than two hundred mu had been recorded as twenty, and two qing ninety-six mu as seventeen.

sentences.zh: 有租稅十有三錢而增至二貫二百者，有租稅二十七錢則增至一貫四百五十者，虔之會昌縣者是也。

translations.literal: There were cases of rent tax of thirteen cash increased to two strings two hundred, and of rent tax of twenty-seven cash increased to one string four hundred fifty—such was Huichang County in Qian.
translations.idiomatic: In Huichang County, Qianzhou, rent of thirteen cash had been raised to two strings two hundred, and rent of twenty-seven cash to one string four hundred fifty.

sentences.zh: 詔望常平使者檢察。

translations.literal: An edict hoped that ever-normal granary commissioners would inspect.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed ever-normal granary commissioners to investigate.

sentences.zh: 」二年，遂詔罷之。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict then abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, the system was abolished by edict.

sentences.zh: 民因方量流徙者，守令招誘歸業；

translations.literal: People who had drifted away because of squaring—the prefects and magistrates were to entice them to return to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates were to encourage people displaced by land measurement to return to their occupations.

sentences.zh: 荒閑田土，召人請佃。

translations.literal: Idle and abandoned land was to summon people to request tenancy.
translations.idiomatic: Abandoned land was to be opened for tenant cultivation.

sentences.zh: 自今諸司毋得起請方田。

translations.literal: From now on, no office might initiate a request for Square Fields.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth no agency could propose reviving Square Fields.

sentences.zh: 諸路已方量者，賦稅不以有無訴論，悉如舊額輸納；

translations.literal: In circuits already squared, tax levies might not be disputed on grounds of presence or absence; all were to pay according to the old quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Where land had already been measured, taxes could no longer be disputed and were to be paid at former quotas.

sentences.zh: 民逃移歸業，已前逋欠稅租，並與除放。

translations.literal: When the people fled and then returned to their occupations, all previously owed tax and rent arrears were to be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Returning refugees were granted remission of all prior tax arrears.

sentences.zh: 賦稅自唐建中初變租庸調法作年支兩稅，夏輸毋過六月，秋輸毋過十一月，遣使分道按率。

translations.literal: Tax levies from the beginning of Jianzhong in Tang, when the zu-yong-diao law was changed to the two tax collections of annual expenditure: summer delivery must not pass the sixth month, autumn delivery must not pass the eleventh month; envoys were sent on separate routes to assess rates.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jianzhong reform of 780, Tang had replaced the zu-yong-diao system with the two-tax system: summer dues by the sixth month, autumn dues by the eleventh, with envoys sent on separate routes to set rates.

sentences.zh: 其弊也，先期而苛斂，增額而繁征，至於五代極矣。

translations.literal: Its abuses were early collection and harsh levies, increasing quotas and multiplying exactions—reaching an extreme in the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Its abuses included premature collection, harsh levies, quota inflation, and multiplying exactions—reaching their worst under the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 宋制歲賦，其類有五：曰公田之賦，凡田之在官，賦民耕而收其租者是也。

translations.literal: Under Song institutions for annual levies, there were five categories: first, the levy on public fields—namely, fields held by the state, levying the people to cultivate and collecting their rent.
translations.idiomatic: Song annual levies fell into five categories: public-field tax on state land rented to cultivators.

sentences.zh: 曰民田之賦，百姓各得專之者是也。

translations.literal: Second, the levy on private fields—namely, what the common people each held exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Private-field tax on land held exclusively by commoners.

sentences.zh: 曰城郭之賦，宅稅、地稅之類是也。

translations.literal: Third, the levy on walled cities and towns—namely, residence tax, land tax, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Urban tax, including residence and land taxes in cities and towns.

sentences.zh: 曰丁口之賦，百姓歲輸身丁錢米是也。

translations.literal: Fourth, the levy on persons and households—namely, the poll tax in cash and grain that commoners paid annually.
translations.idiomatic: Poll tax, the annual head-tax in cash and grain paid by commoners.

sentences.zh: 曰雜變之賦，牛革、蠶鹽之類，隨其所出，變而輸之是也。

translations.literal: Fifth, the levy on miscellaneous commutations—ox hides, silk, salt, and the like, converted according to what was produced and delivered in exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous commutations such as ox hides, silk, and salt, delivered in whatever form local production allowed.

sentences.zh: 歲賦之物，其類有四：曰穀，曰帛，曰金、鐵，曰物產是也。

translations.literal: The articles of annual levies had four categories: grain, silks, gold and iron, and local products.
translations.idiomatic: Annual levy goods fell into four categories: grain, silks, metals, and local products.

sentences.zh: 穀之品七：一曰粟，二曰稻，三曰麥，四曰黍，五曰穄，六曰菽，七曰雜子。

translations.literal: Grain had seven types: first millet, second rice, third wheat, fourth broomcorn millet, fifth panicled millet, sixth beans, seventh miscellaneous seeds.
translations.idiomatic: Grains comprised seven types: millet, rice, wheat, broomcorn millet, panicled millet, beans, and miscellaneous seeds.

sentences.zh: 帛之品十：一曰羅，二曰綾，三曰絹，四曰紗，五曰絁，六曰綢，七曰雜折，八曰絲線，九曰綿，十曰布葛。

translations.literal: Silks had ten types: first gauze, second damask, third silk, fourth gauze weave, fifth coarse silk, sixth silk fabric, seventh miscellaneous folded goods, eighth silk thread, ninth cotton, tenth cloth and hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Silks comprised ten types: gauze, damask, silk, fine gauze, coarse silk, silk fabric, miscellaneous folded goods, silk thread, cotton, and cloth and hemp.

sentences.zh: 金鐵之品四：一曰金，二曰銀，三曰鐵、鑞，四曰銅、鐵錢。

translations.literal: Gold and iron had four types: first gold, second silver, third iron and tin, fourth copper and iron cash.
translations.idiomatic: Metals comprised four types: gold, silver, iron and tin, and copper and iron currency.

sentences.zh: 物產之品六：一曰六畜，二曰齒、革、翎毛，三曰茶、鹽，四曰竹木、麻草、芻菜，五曰果、藥、油、紙、薪、炭、漆、蠟，六曰雜物。

translations.literal: Local products had six types: first the six domestic animals, second ivory, hides, and feathers, third tea and salt, fourth bamboo, timber, hemp, grass, and fodder, fifth fruit, medicine, oil, paper, fuel, charcoal, lacquer, and wax, sixth miscellaneous goods.
translations.idiomatic: Local products comprised six types: livestock; ivory, hides, and feathers; tea and salt; bamboo, timber, hemp, grass, and fodder; fruit, medicine, oil, paper, fuel, charcoal, lacquer, and wax; and miscellaneous goods.

sentences.zh: 其輸有常處，而以有餘補不足，則移此輸彼，移近輸遠，謂之「支移」。

translations.literal: Delivery had fixed places, but using surplus to supplement deficiency meant shifting delivery from here to there, from near to far—this was called "branch transfer."
translations.idiomatic: Though deliveries had fixed destinations, surplus regions could supply deficient ones by shifting goods from place to place or from near to far—called "branch transfer."

sentences.zh: 其入有常物，而一時所輸則變而取之，使其直輕重相當，謂之「折變」。

translations.literal: What was paid in had fixed articles, but what was delivered at a given time was converted and taken so that values light and heavy were equivalent—this was called "commutation."
translations.idiomatic: Though dues were nominally fixed in kind, payments were often converted to equivalent values in other goods—called "commutation."

sentences.zh: 其輸之遲速，視收成早暮而寬為之期，所以紓民力。

translations.literal: The speed of delivery looked to whether the harvest was early or late and set lenient deadlines—thereby easing the people's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Payment deadlines were adjusted to early or late harvests to ease the burden on the populace.

sentences.zh: 諸州歲奏戶帳，具載其丁口，男夫二十為丁，六十為老。

translations.literal: All prefectures annually submitted household registers, fully recording their persons and households; adult males at twenty counted as ding, at sixty as aged.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures submitted annual household registers listing all members; males counted as adult laborers at twenty and as aged at sixty.

sentences.zh: 兩物折科物，非土地所宜而抑配者，禁之。

translations.literal: Commutation of two articles into assessed articles, when not suited to the land and forcibly assigned, was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Forced commutation of unsuitable goods not native to a region was prohibited.

sentences.zh: 五代以來，常檢視見墾田以定歲租。

translations.literal: Since the Five Dynasties, they had regularly inspected visible reclaimed fields to fix annual rent.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Five Dynasties, officials had routinely surveyed visible cultivated land to set annual rent.

sentences.zh: 吏緣為奸，稅不均適，繇是百姓失業，田多荒蕪。

translations.literal: Officials used this as a pretext for fraud; taxes were not evenly apportioned; thereby the common people lost their occupations and fields were largely abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Officials exploited the practice for fraud, taxes fell unevenly, commoners lost their livelihoods, and much land lay fallow.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，詔許民辟土，州縣毋得檢括，止以見佃為額。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, an edict permitted the people to open land; prefectures and counties might not inspect and seize; they were to take only currently tenanted land as the quota.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu ascended the throne, he permitted land reclamation and forbade prefectures and counties from intrusive surveys, fixing quotas only on land already under cultivation.

sentences.zh: 選官分蒞京畿倉瘐，及詣諸道，受民租調，有增羨者輒得罪，多入民租者或至棄市。

translations.literal: Selected officials were sent separately to oversee capital granaries and depots, and to travel to all circuits to receive the people's rent and taxes; those who increased surpluses were immediately punished, and those who took in too much of the people's rent sometimes were executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were dispatched to oversee capital granaries and to collect rent and taxes in the circuits; those who inflated receipts were punished, and those who over-collected sometimes faced execution.

sentences.zh: 舊諸州收稅畢，符屬縣追吏會鈔，縣吏厚斂里胥以賂州之吏，里胥復率於民，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: Formerly, when all prefectures finished collecting taxes, they sent orders to the counties to pursue clerks to meet for tallying receipts; county clerks heavily levied village heads to bribe prefectural clerks, and village heads again assessed the people—the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, after tax collection prefectures ordered counties to send clerks to reconcile receipts; county clerks extorted village heads to bribe prefectural staff, who in turn passed the burden to commoners.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年，乃下詔禁止。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong, an edict then forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 4, an edict prohibited the practice.

sentences.zh: 令諸州受租籍不得稱分、毫、合、龠、銖、厘、絲、忽，錢必成文，絹帛成尺，粟成升，絲綿成兩，薪蒿成束，金銀成錢。

translations.literal: It ordered all prefectures, when receiving rent registers, not to use fen, hao, ge, yue, zhu, li, si, or hu; cash must be in whole strings, silk in whole chi, grain in whole sheng, silk floss in whole liang, fuel and weeds in whole bundles, gold and silver in whole amounts of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures were forbidden to record fractional units on rent registers; cash had to be in whole strings, silk in whole chi, grain in whole sheng, floss in whole liang, fuel in whole bundles, and gold and silver in standard cash amounts.

sentences.zh: 綢不滿半匹、絹不滿一匹者，許計丈尺輸直，無得三戶、五戶聚合成匹，送納煩擾。

translations.literal: When silk fabric did not reach half a bolt or silk did not reach one bolt, payment by measured length in cash value was permitted; they might not combine three or five households into one bolt for delivery, causing troublesome submission.
translations.idiomatic: Shortfalls under half a bolt of silk fabric or one bolt of silk could be paid in cash by measured length; combining partial dues from several households into one bolt was forbidden as too burdensome.

sentences.zh: 民輸夏稅，所在遣縣尉部弓手於要路巡護，後聞擾民，罷之，止令鄉耆、壯丁防援。

translations.literal: When the people delivered summer tax, everywhere the assistant magistrate led bowmen to patrol key roads; later it was heard that this harassed the people, so it was abolished, and only village elders and strong youths were ordered to guard and escort.
translations.idiomatic: When commoners delivered summer tax, assistant magistrates had once deployed bowmen to patrol key roads; learning this harassed the people, the court abolished the practice and left escort duty to village elders and militia.

sentences.zh: 諸州稅籍，錄事參軍按視，判官振舉。

translations.literal: Tax registers in all prefectures were inspected by the recording secretary and urged by the judicial administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural tax registers were inspected by recording secretaries and overseen by judicial administrators.

sentences.zh: 形勢戶立別籍，通判專掌督之，二稅須於三限前半月畢輸。

translations.literal: Powerful households had separate registers; the vice-prefect was solely in charge of supervising them; both taxes had to be fully paid half a month before the three deadlines.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful households were listed on separate registers supervised by vice-prefects, and both taxes had to be paid in full half a month before the three deadlines.

sentences.zh: 歲起納二稅，前期令縣各造稅籍，具一縣戶數、夏秋稅苗畝桑功及緣科物為帳一，送州覆校定，用州印，藏長吏廳，縣籍亦用州印，給付令佐。

translations.literal: Each year when the two taxes began, beforehand each county was ordered to compile tax registers, setting forth in one ledger the county's household count, summer and autumn tax seedlings, mu, mulberry yield, and attached assessed articles; this was sent to the prefecture for review and fixing, sealed with the prefectural stamp, stored in the chief official's hall; county registers also used the prefectural stamp and were given to magistrates and assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Before each year's two tax collections, counties compiled registers listing households, summer and autumn assessments, acreage, mulberry yields, and attached dues; prefectures reviewed, sealed, and stored them, issuing stamped copies to magistrates.

sentences.zh: 造夏稅籍以正月一日，秋稅籍以四月一日，並限四十五日畢。

translations.literal: Summer tax registers were compiled starting the first day of the first month; autumn tax registers starting the first day of the fourth month; both were limited to forty-five days for completion.
translations.idiomatic: Summer tax registers were compiled from the first day of the first month, autumn registers from the first day of the fourth month, each within forty-five days.

sentences.zh: 開封府等七十州夏稅，舊以五月十五日起納，七月三十日畢。

translations.literal: For Kaifeng Prefecture and seventy other prefectures, summer tax formerly began collection on the fifteenth day of the fifth month and ended on the thirtieth day of the seventh month.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaifeng Prefecture and seventy other prefectures, summer tax collection formerly ran from the fifteenth day of the fifth month through the thirtieth day of the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 河北、河東諸州氣候差晚，五月十五日起納，八月五日畢。

translations.literal: In Hebei and Hedong prefectures the climate was somewhat late; collection began the fifteenth day of the fifth month and ended the fifth day of the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: In Hebei and Hedong, where the climate was later, collection ran from the fifteenth day of the fifth month through the fifth day of the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 潁州等一十三州及淮南、江南、兩浙、福建、廣南、荊湖、川峽五月一日起納，七月十五日畢。

translations.literal: Yingzhou and twelve other prefectures, and Huainan, Jiangnan, the two Zhe circuits, Fujian, Guangnan, Jinghu, and Chuanxia began collection on the first day of the fifth month and ended on the fifteenth day of the seventh month.
translations.idiomatic: In Yingzhou and twelve other prefectures, plus Huainan, Jiangnan, the two Zhe circuits, Fujian, Guangnan, Jinghu, and Sichuan, collection ran from the first day of the fifth month through the fifteenth day of the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 秋稅自九月一日起納，十二月十五日畢，後又並加一月或值閏月，其田蠶亦有早晚不同，有司臨時奏裁。

translations.literal: Autumn tax began collection on the first day of the ninth month and ended on the fifteenth day of the twelfth month; later one month was added in all cases, or when there was an intercalary month; fields and silkworms also had early and late differences, and the responsible offices submitted for temporary imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn tax collection ran from the first day of the ninth month through the fifteenth day of the twelfth month; later an extra month was often allowed, and deadlines were adjusted for intercalary months and regional differences in harvest and sericulture.

sentences.zh: 繼而以河北、河東諸州秋稅多輸邊郡，常限外更加一月。

translations.literal: Subsequently, because autumn tax in Hebei and Hedong prefectures was largely delivered to border prefectures, one month beyond the usual deadline was regularly added.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hebei and Hedong autumn taxes were largely shipped to border prefectures, an extra month beyond the usual deadline was regularly granted.

sentences.zh: 江南、兩浙、荊湖、廣南、福建土多粳稻，須霜降成實，自十月一日始收租。

translations.literal: Jiangnan, the two Zhe circuits, Jinghu, Guangnan, and Fujian had mostly japonica rice; it had to ripen after frost descent, so rent collection began on the first day of the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangnan, the two Zhe circuits, Jinghu, Guangnan, and Fujian, where japonica rice ripened only after frost, rent collection began on the first day of the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 掌納官吏以限外欠數，差定其罰。

translations.literal: Officials in charge of collection, for shortfalls beyond the deadline, had punishments set by degree.
translations.idiomatic: Collecting officials faced graded penalties for shortfalls beyond the deadline.

sentences.zh: 限前畢，減選，升資。

translations.literal: If completed before the deadline, selection cycles were reduced and rank advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Completion before the deadline brought accelerated promotion.

sentences.zh: 民逋租逾限，取保歸辦，母得禁係。

translations.literal: When the people were in arrears on rent beyond the deadline, they might give surety and return to settle; they must not be imprisoned and bound.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners in rent arrears beyond the deadline could give surety and return home to settle; they could not be imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 中國租二十石輸牛革一，準錢千。

translations.literal: In central China, for every twenty shi of rent one ox hide was delivered, valued at one thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: In central China, one ox hide was due for every twenty shi of rent, valued at one thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 川蜀尚循舊制，牛驢死，革盡入官，乃詔蠲之，定民租二百石輸牛革一，準錢千五百。

translations.literal: Sichuan still followed the old system: when oxen and donkeys died, all hides went to the state; then an edict remitted this, fixing that for every two hundred shi of private rent one ox hide was delivered, valued at one thousand five hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan still followed the old rule that all hides from dead oxen and donkeys went to the state; an edict abolished this and set one ox hide per two hundred shi of rent, valued at one thousand five hundred cash.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，江西轉運使言：「本路蠶桑數少，而金價頗低。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, the Jiangxi transport commissioner said: In this circuit mulberry and silkworm production is scant, while the price of gold is rather low.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2, the Jiangxi transport commissioner reported that the circuit had little mulberry and sericulture while gold prices were relatively low.

sentences.zh: 今折徵，絹估少而傷民，金估多而傷官。

translations.literal: Now for commuted collection, silk assessed low harms the people, while gold assessed high harms the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Under the current commutation system, undervaluing silk hurt commoners while overvaluing gold hurt the treasury.

sentences.zh: 金上等舊估兩十千，今請估八千；

translations.literal: For top-grade gold, the old estimate was twenty thousand per liang; now it is requested to assess it at eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Top-grade gold had been assessed at twenty thousand cash per liang; he asked that it be reassessed at eight thousand.

sentences.zh: 絹上等舊估匹一千，今請估一千三百，餘以次增損。

translations.literal: For top-grade silk, the old estimate was one thousand per bolt; now it is requested to assess it at one thousand three hundred; the rest to be increased or decreased in order.
translations.idiomatic: Top-grade silk had been assessed at one thousand cash per bolt; he proposed raising it to thirteen hundred, with other grades adjusted proportionally.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，以刑部員外、直史館陳靖為京畿均田使，聽自擇京朝官，分縣據元額定稅，不得增收剩數；

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping, Chen Jing, Vice Minister of Justice and Direct Historian of the History Institute, was made Equal-Fields Commissioner for the Capital Region; he was permitted to choose capital officials himself, dividing by county and fixing tax according to original quotas, not permitted to increase and collect surplus amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 3, Chen Jing—Vice Minister of Justice and Institute Historian—was appointed Equal-Fields Commissioner for the capital region. He could select metropolitan officials himself, set taxes county by county at original quotas, and was forbidden to collect any surplus.

sentences.zh: 逃戶別立籍，令本府招誘歸業；

translations.literal: Absentee households were entered on separate registers; the prefecture was ordered to entice them back to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitive households were listed on separate rolls, and local prefectures were instructed to induce them to return to farming.

sentences.zh: 桑功更不均檢，民戶廣令種植。

translations.literal: Mulberry quotas were further not evenly inspected; broad orders were issued to households to plant.
translations.idiomatic: Mulberry quotas were no longer uniformly assessed, and households were broadly ordered to plant more mulberry trees.

sentences.zh: 尋聞居民弗諭朝旨，翦伐桑柘，即詔罷之。

translations.literal: Soon it was heard that residents did not understand the court's intent and cut down mulberry and paper-mulberry trees; an edict immediately abolished the policy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long it was reported that residents, misunderstanding the court's intent, were cutting down mulberry trees; the policy was immediately canceled.

sentences.zh: 六年，罷廣南西路轉運使馮漣上言：「廉、橫、賓、白州民雖墾田，未嘗輸送，已命官檢括，令盡出常租。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, after removing Guangnan West Circuit transport commissioner Feng Lian, a memorial stated: The people of Lian, Heng, Bin, and Bai prefectures, though they cultivate fields, have never delivered tribute; officials have already been ordered to inspect and register them, commanding them to pay full regular rent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, after dismissing Guangnan West transport commissioner Feng Lian, a memorial stated: In Lian, Heng, Bin, and Bai prefectures, farmers who had cleared land had never paid taxes; officials had been ordered to investigate and collect full standard rent.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「遠方之民，宜省徭賦。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. The Emperor said: For people of distant regions, corvée and levies should be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Frontier subjects deserve lighter corvée and tax burdens."

sentences.zh: 」亟命停罷。

translations.literal: Closing quotation; he urgently ordered it stopped and abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered the measure halted.

sentences.zh: 知袁州何蒙請以金折本州二稅，真宗曰：「若是，將盡廢耕農矣。

translations.literal: He Meng, prefect of Yuanzhou, requested that the two taxes of this prefecture be commuted in gold; Emperor Zhenzong said: If so, farming would be entirely abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhou prefect He Meng proposed commuting the prefecture's two seasonal land taxes into gold. Emperor Zhenzong said: "At that rate, agriculture would disappear entirely."

sentences.zh: 」不許。

translations.literal: Closing quotation; not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，連歲豐稔，邊儲有備，河北諸路稅賦，並聽於本州軍輸納。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu, with successive years of abundant harvests and frontier stores prepared, tax levies of all Hebei circuits were all permitted to be delivered at their own prefectures and garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu era, after years of good harvests had filled frontier granaries, Hebei circuits were allowed to pay taxes locally rather than ship them elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 二年，頒《幕職州縣官招徠戶口旌賞條製》。

translations.literal: In the second year, the 《Regulations on Rewards for Recruiting Households by Administrative and County Officials》 was promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, the court issued the 《Regulations on Rewards for Administrative and County Officials Who Recruited Households》.

sentences.zh: 舊制，縣吏能招增戶口者，縣即升等，乃加其奉；

translations.literal: Under the old system, when county clerks could recruit and increase population, the county was immediately promoted in grade, and their salaries were increased.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, counties whose clerks added registered households were promoted in rank and their officials received higher salaries.

sentences.zh: 至有析客戶為主戶者，雖登於籍，而賦稅無所增。

translations.literal: To the point that some split tenant households into primary households; though registered on the rolls, tax and levies increased not at all.
translations.idiomatic: Some counties even split tenant households into primary ones—adding names to the register without increasing revenue.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔禁之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, an edict banned the practice.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，嘗詔荊湖等路民輸丁錢，未成丁、已入老並身有廢疾者，免之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi, an edict had ordered the people of Jinghu and other circuits to pay poll money; those not yet adult, already aged, and those with physical disabilities were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongxi, the court had required Jinghu and related circuits to pay the adult poll tax, exempting minors, the elderly, and the disabled.

sentences.zh: 至是，又除兩浙、福建、荊湖、廣南舊輸身丁錢，歲凡四十五萬四百貫。

translations.literal: At this time, the old body-and-poll money paid by Liangzhe, Fujian, Jinghu, and Guangnan was again abolished, totaling four hundred fifty thousand and four hundred strings per year.
translations.idiomatic: Now the court also abolished the legacy poll taxes in Liangzhe, Fujian, Jinghu, and Guangnan—450,400 strings per year.

sentences.zh: 九年，詔諸路支移稅賦勿至兩次，仍許以粟、麥、蕎、菽互相折輸。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, an edict ordered that redirected tax levies on all circuits should not reach two times, and still permitted mutual conversion delivery of millet, wheat, buckwheat, and beans.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, edicts limited tax redirection to no more than two transfers and allowed millet, wheat, buckwheat, and beans to be commuted for one another.

sentences.zh: 凡歲賦，穀以石計，錢以緡計，帛以匹計，金銀、絲綿以兩計，槁秸、薪蒸以圍計，他物各以其數計。

translations.literal: As to annual levies in general: grain was counted by shi, cash by string, cloth by bolt, gold and silver and silk floss by liang, straw and firewood by bundle, other goods each by their number.
translations.idiomatic: Annual levies were measured in shi for grain, strings of cash for money, bolts for cloth, taels for gold, silver, and silk floss, bundles for straw and firewood, and appropriate units for all other goods.

sentences.zh: 至道末，總七千八十九萬三千；

translations.literal: At the end of Zhidao, the total was seventy million eight hundred ninety thousand three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Zhidao era, the total reached 70,893,000 units.

sentences.zh: 天禧五年，視至道之數有增有減，總六千四百五十三萬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianxi, compared with the Zhidao figures there were increases and decreases; the total was sixty-four million five hundred thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxi 5, revenue had risen and fallen in various categories compared with Zhidao, totaling 64,530,000.

sentences.zh: 其折變及移輸比壤者，則視當時所須焉。

translations.literal: As for conversion and redirected delivery to neighboring regions, these depended on what was needed at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Conversions and cross-region deliveries varied according to immediate need.

sentences.zh: 宋克平諸國，每以恤民為先務，累朝相承，凡無名苛細之斂，常加剗革，尺縑鬥粟，未聞有所增益。

translations.literal: When Song conquered the various states, relieving the people was always the first task; successive reigns inherited this; all nameless harsh and minute exactions were constantly cut and reformed; not even an inch of silk or a peck of grain was heard to have been added.
translations.idiomatic: From its conquest of rival states, the Song placed popular welfare first. Dynasty after dynasty canceled obscure petty levies, and not even a bolt of silk or a peck of grain was knowingly added to the burden.

sentences.zh: 一遇水旱徭役，則蠲除倚格，殆無虛歲，倚格者後或凶歉，亦輒蠲之。

translations.literal: Whenever there were floods, droughts, or corvée labor, remissions and deferred installments followed—almost no year went unused; those on deferred payment, if later there was famine, were also immediately remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Flood, drought, or corvée duty routinely brought remissions and deferred installments—hardly a year passed without relief—and deferred payments were canceled again whenever famine followed.

sentences.zh: 而又田製不立川畝轉易，丁口隱漏，兼並冒偽，未嘗考按，故賦入之利視前代為薄。

translations.literal: Yet furthermore, field systems were not established, fields and mu changed hands easily, household members were concealed and omitted, mergers and fraud went unexamined, so revenue gain was thin compared with previous dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Yet land registers were never systematically maintained, fields changed hands freely, households were undercounted, and consolidation fraud went unchecked—so tax income remained thinner than in earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 丁謂嘗言：二十而稅一者有之，三十而稅一者有之。

translations.literal: Ding Wei once said: There were cases of one part in twenty taxed, and cases of one part in thirty taxed.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei once observed that effective tax rates ranged from one-twentieth to one-thirtieth of yield.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嗣位，首寬畿縣田賦，詔三等以下戶毋遠輸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong succeeded to the throne, he first relaxed capital-region land tax; an edict ordered that households of the third grade and below should not deliver at distant points.
translations.idiomatic: Upon Renzong's accession, he first eased land taxes in the capital region, decreeing that households below the third grade need not ship payments long distances.

sentences.zh: 河中府、同華州請免支移，帝以問輔臣，對曰：「西鄙宿兵，非移用民賦則軍食不足。

translations.literal: Hezhong Prefecture and Tong and Hua prefectures requested exemption from redirected delivery; the Emperor asked his chief ministers; they replied: Troops are long stationed on the western frontier; without redirecting the people's levies, army provisions would be insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong Prefecture and Tong and Hua prefectures asked to be exempt from tax redirection. When the emperor consulted his ministers, they replied: "Troops remain stationed on the western frontier; without redirecting local taxes, the army would go hungry."

sentences.zh: 」特詔量減支移。

translations.literal: Closing quotation; a special edict ordered redirected delivery to be reduced by measure.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict ordered a measured reduction in redirected deliveries.

sentences.zh: 福州王氏時有田千餘頃，謂之「官莊「，自太平興國中授券予民耕，歲使輸賦。

translations.literal: In Fuzhou the Wang clan at one time had more than a thousand qing of fields, called the "Official Estate"; since Taiping Xingguo, tickets were granted to the people to cultivate, and each year they were made to pay tax.
translations.idiomatic: In Fuzhou the Wang clan once held more than a thousand qing of land known as the "Official Estate." Since Taiping Xingguo, farmers had been given leases to cultivate it and pay annual rent.

sentences.zh: 至是，發運使方仲荀言：「此公田也，鬻之可得厚利。

translations.literal: At this time, the transport commissioner Fang Zhongxun said: This is public land; selling it could obtain substantial profit.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner Fang Zhongxun proposed: "This is public land; selling it would yield a substantial profit."

sentences.zh: 」遣尚書屯田員外郎幸惟慶領其事，凡售錢三十五萬餘緡，詔減緡錢三之一，期三年畢償。

translations.literal: Closing quotation; Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue's Colonization Office Xing Weiqing was dispatched to oversee the matter; in all the sale money was more than three hundred fifty thousand strings; an edict reduced cash strings by one-third, with a deadline of three years for full repayment.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Vice Director of Colonization Xing Weiqing to manage the sale, which brought in more than 350,000 strings. Leaseholders were granted a one-third reduction, payable over three years.

sentences.zh: 監察御史朱諫以為傷民，不可。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Zhu Jian held that it harmed the people and could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Zhu Jian argued that the scheme harmed commoners and should not proceed.

sentences.zh: 即而期盡，未償者猶十二萬八千餘緡，詔悉蠲之。

translations.literal: Immediately afterward the deadline expired; those not yet repaid still amounted to more than one hundred twenty-eight thousand strings; an edict remitted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: When the three-year term expired, more than 128,000 strings remained unpaid; the court remitted the entire balance.

sentences.zh: 後又詔公田重復取賦者皆罷。

translations.literal: Later another edict ordered that all repeated collection of tax on public land be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Later edicts ended all duplicate taxation of public land.

sentences.zh: 天聖時，貝州言：「民析居者例加稅，謂之『罰稅』，他州無此比。

translations.literal: During Tiansheng, Beizhou reported: When the people divided households, tax was routinely added, called the "penalty tax"; other prefectures had no such precedent.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiansheng, Beizhou reported: "When households split, they were routinely hit with an extra levy called a 'penalty tax'—a practice unknown elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 」詔除之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation; an edict abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict abolished the levy.

sentences.zh: 自是，州縣有言稅之苛細無名者，蠲損甚眾。

translations.literal: From this, when prefectures and counties reported harsh, minute, and nameless taxes, remissions and reductions were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever local officials reported obscure or petty taxes, remissions became frequent.

sentences.zh: 自唐以來，民計田輸賦外，增取他物，復折為賦，謂之「雜變」，亦謂之「沿納」。

translations.literal: Since Tang times, beyond what the people counted on fields and paid in tax, other goods were additionally taken and again converted into levies, called "miscellaneous conversion," also called "supplementary delivery."
translations.idiomatic: Since Tang times, beyond standard land tax, officials collected other goods and converted them into levies known as "miscellaneous conversions" or "supplementary deliveries."

sentences.zh: 而名品煩細，其類不一。

translations.literal: Yet the named items were numerous and minute; the categories were not one.
translations.idiomatic: The items were countless and varied.

sentences.zh: 官司歲附帳籍，並緣侵優，民以為患。

translations.literal: Each year official offices attached account registers, all leveraging encroachment and overreach; the people regarded it as an affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Each year officials appended new items to the tax rolls, exploiting every loophole—a perennial grievance for taxpayers.

sentences.zh: 明道中，帝躬耕籍田，因詔三司以類並合。

translations.literal: In Mingdao, the Emperor personally plowed the ceremonial field; he therefore ordered the Three Departments to merge by category.
translations.idiomatic: During Mingdao, after the emperor performed the ceremonial plowing, he ordered the Three Departments to consolidate levies by category.

sentences.zh: 於是悉除諸名品，並為一物，夏秋歲入，第分粗細二色，百姓便之。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the various named items were entirely abolished and merged into one item; summer and autumn annual receipts were only divided into coarse and fine two grades; the common people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: All separate items were abolished and combined into a single levy, with summer and autumn payments distinguished only as coarse or fine grade—a reform the people welcomed.

sentences.zh: 州縣賦入有籍，歲一置，謂之空行簿，以待歲中催科；

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties had registers for levy receipts; one was set up each year, called the provisional register, to await mid-year collection.
translations.idiomatic: Each county kept tax registers renewed annually in a "provisional ledger" used for mid-year collection.

sentences.zh: 閏年別置，謂之實行簿，以藏有司。

translations.literal: In intercalary years a separate one was set up, called the permanent register, stored with the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: In leap years a separate "permanent ledger" was compiled and kept in official archives.

sentences.zh: 天聖初，或言實行簿無用，而率民錢為擾，罷之。

translations.literal: Early in Tiansheng, someone said the permanent register was useless and that collecting money from the people was a nuisance; it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiansheng, critics called the permanent ledger useless and its fees a burden on taxpayers; it was abolished.

sentences.zh: 景祐元年，侍御史韓瀆言：「天下賦入之繁，但存催科一簿，一有散亡，則耗登之數無從鉤考。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyou, Attendant Censor Han Du said: The levies of the empire are complex; yet only the collection register remains; once lost, the recorded figures cannot be audited.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyou 1, Attendant Censor Han Du warned: "Tax revenue is complex nationwide, yet only a single collection ledger survives. If it is lost, revenue figures cannot be audited."

sentences.zh: 請復置實行簿。

translations.literal: He requested that the permanent register be restored.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the permanent ledger be restored.

sentences.zh: 」詔再閏一造。

translations.literal: Closing quotation; an edict ordered one to be made every second intercalary year.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the ledger compiled once every two leap years.

sentences.zh: 至慶曆中復故。

translations.literal: By the Qingli era it reverted to the former practice.
translations.idiomatic: By the Qingli era the old practice was restored.

sentences.zh: 時患州縣賦役之煩，詔諸路上其數，俾二府大臣合議蠲減。

translations.literal: At the time distressed by the burdens of prefecture and county levies and corvée, an edict ordered all circuits to submit their figures, enabling the two-faction great ministers jointly to discuss remission and reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Concerned about local tax and corvée burdens, the court ordered every circuit to report figures so the chief ministers could jointly decide reductions.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「稅籍有偽書逃徙，或因推割，用幸走移，若請占公田而不輸稅。

translations.literal: Another edict said: In tax registers there are forged records and flight; or through land partition surveys, they take advantage to shift away; or they request allocation of public land yet do not pay tax.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared: "Tax registers are riddled with fraud—false records, flight, evasion through land transfers, and occupation of public land without payment."

sentences.zh: 如此之類，縣令、佐能究見其弊，以增賦入，量數議賞。

translations.literal: Cases such as these: if magistrates and assistants can thoroughly expose the abuses and increase levy receipts, rewards should be discussed according to the amount.
translations.idiomatic: "Magistrates who uncover such abuses and increase revenue shall be rewarded in proportion to the gain."

sentences.zh: 」既而諫官王素言：「天下田賦輕重不等，請均定。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. Soon thereafter Remonstrance Official Wang Su said: Land taxes across the empire are unequal in weight; equalization is requested.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Official Wang Su soon followed up: "Land taxes vary unevenly nationwide; please equalize them."

sentences.zh: 」而歐陽修亦言：「秘書丞孫琳嘗往洺州肥鄉縣，與大理寺丞郭諮以千步方田法括定民田，願詔二人得任之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. And Ouyang Xiu also said: Secretariat Director Sun Lin once went to Feixiang County in Mozhou, and with Court of Judicial Review Director Guo Zi used the thousand-pace square-field method to survey and fix the people's fields; he wished that an edict authorize the two men to undertake the task.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu added: "Secretariat Director Sun Lin and Court of Judicial Review Director Guo Zi once surveyed farmland in Feixiang County, Mozhou, using the thousand-pace square-field method. Both should be empowered to carry this work forward."

sentences.zh: 」三司亦以為然，且請於亳、壽、蔡、汝四州擇庀不均者均之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. The Three Departments also deemed it so, and further requested that in Bozhou, Shouzhou, Caizhou, and Ruzhou, where uneven, those be selected and equalized.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments agreed and proposed equalizing the most uneven districts in Bozhou, Shou, Cai, and Ru prefectures.

sentences.zh: 於是遣諮蔡州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guo Zi was dispatched to Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zi was then sent to Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 諮首括一縣，得田二萬六千九百三十餘頃，均其賦於民。

translations.literal: Guo Zi first surveyed one county, obtaining more than twenty-six thousand nine hundred thirty qing of fields, and equalized the levies among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zi first surveyed one county, registering more than 26,930 qing of land and equalizing tax burdens among local households.

sentences.zh: 既而諮言州縣多逃田，未可盡括，朝廷亦重勞人，遂罷。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter Guo Zi said that prefectures and counties had much abandoned land and it could not all be surveyed; the court also weighed the burden on the people; thus it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zi soon reported that widespread abandoned land made complete surveying impossible, and the court, wary of overburdening the populace, abandoned the project.

sentences.zh: 陝西、河東用兵，民賦率多支移，因增取地裏腳錢，民不能堪。

translations.literal: When campaigns were fought in Shaanxi and Hedong, the people's levies were mostly redirected; accordingly the overland transport surcharge was additionally collected; the people could not endure it.
translations.idiomatic: Military campaigns in Shaanxi and Hedong drove frequent tax redirection, and officials added overland transport surcharges that people could not bear.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔陝西特蠲之，且令後勿復取。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict specially remitted it in Shaanxi, and ordered that henceforth it not again be collected.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Shaanxi was granted a special remission, and future collection was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 既而詔河東亦然。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter an edict ordered Hedong likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong received the same order shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 又令諸路轉運司：「支移、折變，前期半歲書於榜以諭民，有未便者聽自言，主者裁之。

translations.literal: It was further ordered to transport commissioners of all circuits: For redirected delivery and conversion, half a year in advance write on placards to inform the people; those who find it inconvenient are permitted to state it themselves; the responsible official decides.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioners were further instructed: "Post redirected-delivery and conversion plans six months in advance. Anyone inconvenienced may petition, and responsible officials shall decide."

sentences.zh: 」皇祐中，詔：「廣西賦布，匹為錢二百。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. In Huangyou, an edict: Guangxi tribute cloth, each bolt valued at two hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangyou, an edict fixed Guangxi tribute cloth at two hundred cash per bolt.

sentences.zh: 如聞有司擅損其價，重困遠人，宜令復故。

translations.literal: As heard, responsible offices on their own authority reduced the price, heavily distressing people of distant regions; it should be ordered restored to the former rate.
translations.idiomatic: "We hear officials have been cutting the price on their own, crushing distant subjects. Restore the original rate."

sentences.zh: 」州郡歲常先奏雨足歲豐，後雖災害，不敢上聞，故民賦罕得蠲者，乃下詔申飭之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. Prefectures and commanderies each year routinely first reported abundant rain and rich harvest; afterward even when there were disasters, they dared not report upward, so the people's levies rarely received remission; then an edict was issued to admonish them.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures habitually reported good rains and bumper harvests early each year, then withheld disaster reports—so tax remissions were rare. The court issued stern admonitions.

sentences.zh: 又損開封諸縣田賦，視舊額十之三，命著於法。

translations.literal: Also the land tax of the various counties of Kaifeng was reduced, to three-tenths of the old quota; an order was given to inscribe it in law.
translations.idiomatic: Land taxes in Kaifeng counties were cut to thirty percent of old quotas and written into law.

sentences.zh: 支移、折變，貧弱者尤以為患。

translations.literal: Redirected delivery and conversion—the poor and weak especially regarded them as an affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Redirected delivery and commutation weighed heaviest on the poor.

sentences.zh: 景祐初，嘗詔戶在第九等免之，後孤獨戶亦皆免。

translations.literal: Early in Jingyou, an edict had exempted households in the ninth grade; later solitary households were also all exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingyou, ninth-grade households were exempted; later solitary households were exempted as well.

sentences.zh: 至是，因下赦書，責轉運司裁損，歲終條上。

translations.literal: At this time, through issuing an amnesty edict, transport commissioners were charged to cut and reduce, and at year's end submit itemized reports upward.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty edict then charged transport commissioners to trim abuses and file itemized reports at year's end.

sentences.zh: 其後赦書數以為言，又令折科為平估，毋得害農。

translations.literal: Thereafter amnesty edicts repeatedly spoke of this; it was again ordered that conversion collection use fair valuation, and must not harm farming.
translations.idiomatic: Later amnesties repeated the command: commutation must use fair valuation and must not harm farmers.

sentences.zh: 久之，復詔曰：「如聞諸路比言折科民賦，多以所折復變他物，或增取其直，重困良農。

translations.literal: After a long time, another edict said: As heard, on all circuits, comparing reports on conversion collection of the people's levies, many take what was converted and again change it to other goods, or increase and take its value, heavily distressing good farmers.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, another edict complained: "We hear that across the circuits, commuted taxes are often converted again into other goods or marked up in price, crushing honest farmers."

sentences.zh: 雖屢戒敕，莫能奉宣詔令。

translations.literal: Although repeatedly admonished by edict, none could faithfully carry out and proclaim the imperial orders.
translations.idiomatic: "Repeated edicts have failed to restrain them."

sentences.zh: 自今有此，州長吏即時上聞。

translations.literal: From now on, whenever there is this, the prefectural chief official immediately reports upward.
translations.idiomatic: "Henceforth, any such abuse must be reported immediately by the prefect."

sentences.zh: 」 然有司規聚斂，罕能承帝意焉。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. Yet the responsible offices schemed for aggregation and collection; few could inherit the Emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet revenue officials remained fixated on extraction, and few heeded the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 初，湖、廣、閩、浙因舊制歲斂丁身錢米，大中祥符間，詔除丁錢，而米輸如故。

translations.literal: Initially, Huguang, Fujian, and Zhejiang following the old system collected poll money and rice annually; during Dazhong Xiangfu, an edict abolished poll money, but rice delivery remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Hu, Guang, Fujian, and Zhejiang had long collected annual poll taxes in cash and rice. During Dazhong Xiangfu the cash component was abolished, but rice payments continued.

sentences.zh: 至天聖中，始並除婺、秀二州丁錢。

translations.literal: By Tiansheng, the poll money of Wu and Xiu prefectures was first altogether abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Not until Tiansheng were poll taxes in Wu and Xiu prefectures fully abolished.

sentences.zh: 後龐籍請罷漳、泉、興化軍丁米，有司持不可。

translations.literal: Later Pang Ji requested abolishing the poll rice of Zhang, Quan, and Xinghua Garrison; the responsible offices maintained it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Later Pang Ji proposed abolishing poll rice in Zhang, Quan, and Xinghua—but the responsible offices refused.

sentences.zh: 皇祐三年，帝命三司首減郴永州、桂陽監丁米，以最下數一歲為準，歲減十餘萬石。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangyou, the Emperor ordered the Three Departments first to reduce the poll rice of Chen and Yong prefectures and Guiyang Supervisorate, taking the lowest figure of one year as standard; more than one hundred thousand shi were reduced per year.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangyou 3, the emperor ordered the Three Departments to cut poll rice in Chen, Yong, and Guiyang to the lowest annual figure, saving more than 100,000 shi per year.

sentences.zh: 既而漳、泉、興化亦第損之。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter Zhang, Quan, and Xinghua were also reduced by grade.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, Quan, and Xinghua soon received proportional reductions as well.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐四年，復命轉運司裁定郴、永、桂陽、衡、道州所輸丁米及錢絹雜物，無業者馳之，有業者減半；

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiayou, transport commissioners were again ordered to fix the poll rice, cash, silk, and miscellaneous goods delivered by Chen, Yong, Guiyang, Heng, and Dao prefectures; those without occupation were released from it; those with occupation had half reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou 4, transport commissioners were ordered to fix poll rice, cash, silk, and miscellaneous levies in Chen, Yong, Guiyang, Heng, and Dao: the landless were fully exempt, landholders paid half.

sentences.zh: 後雖進丁，勿復增取。

translations.literal: Even if later there were new adult males, do not again increase collection.
translations.idiomatic: Even when new adult males were registered, no additional levies could be imposed.

sentences.zh: 時廣南猶或輸丁錢，亦命轉運司條上。

translations.literal: At the time Guangnan still sometimes paid poll money; transport commissioners were also ordered to submit itemized reports upward.
translations.idiomatic: Guangnan still paid some poll taxes, and transport commissioners were ordered to report figures for reduction.

sentences.zh: 自是所輸無幾矣。

translations.literal: From this the amount delivered was not much.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the burden was negligible.

sentences.zh: 自郭諮均稅之法罷，論者謂朝廷徒恤一時之勞，而失經遠之慮。

translations.literal: Since Guo Zi's equal-tax method was abolished, critics said the court merely spared momentary labor yet lost far-reaching forethought.
translations.idiomatic: After Guo Zi's equal-tax reforms were abandoned, critics charged that the court had spared short-term hardship at the cost of long-term fiscal soundness.

sentences.zh: 至皇祐中，天下墾田視景德增四十一萬七千餘頃，而歲入九穀乃減七十一萬八千餘石，蓋田賦不均，其弊如此。

translations.literal: By Huangyou, tilled fields empire-wide compared with Jingde had increased by more than four hundred seventeen thousand qing, yet annual receipt of the nine grains decreased by more than seven hundred eighteen thousand shi—such were the harms of unequal land tax.
translations.idiomatic: By Huangyou, cultivated land had grown by more than 417,000 qing since Jingde, yet grain tax receipts had fallen by more than 718,000 shi—the cost of unequal land taxation.

sentences.zh: 後田京知滄州，均無棣田，蔡挺知博州，均聊城、高塘田；

translations.literal: Later Tian Jing, as prefect of Cangzhou, equalized fields in Wudi; Cai Ting, as prefect of Bozhou, equalized fields in Liaocheng and Gaotang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Cangzhou prefect Tian Jing equalized land in Wudi, and Bozhou prefect Cai Ting did the same in Liaocheng and Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 歲增賦穀帛之類，無棣總一千一百五十二，聊城、高塘總萬四千八百四十七，而滄州之民不以為便，詔輸如舊。

translations.literal: Annual increases in levies of grain, cloth, and the like: Wudi totaled one thousand one hundred fifty-two; Liaocheng and Gaotang totaled fourteen thousand eight hundred forty-seven; yet the people of Cangzhou did not regard it as convenient; an edict ordered payment as before.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi gained 1,152 units of grain and cloth, Liaocheng and Gaotang 14,847—but Cangzhou residents found the changes burdensome, and the court restored the old rates.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐五年，復詔均定，遣官分行諸路，而秘書丞高本在遣中，獨以為不可均，才均數郡田而止。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiayou, equalization was again ordered by edict; officials were dispatched to travel the various circuits; among those dispatched, Secretariat Director Gao Ben alone held that equalization was impossible, and only a few prefectures' fields were equalized before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou 5, the court again ordered equalization and dispatched officials circuit by circuit. Secretariat Director Gao Ben, among them, argued equalization was impossible, and the effort stopped after only a few prefectures.

sentences.zh: 景德中，賦入之數總四千九百一十六萬九千九百，至皇祐中，增四百四十一萬八千六百六十五，治平中，又增一千四百一十七萬九千三百六十四。

translations.literal: In Jingde, total levy figures were forty-nine million one hundred sixty-nine thousand nine hundred; by Huangyou, an increase of four million four hundred eighteen thousand six hundred sixty-five; in Zhiping, another increase of fourteen million one hundred seventy-nine thousand three hundred sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde revenue totaled 49,169,900; by Huangyou it had risen by 4,418,665; by Zhiping by another 14,179,364.

sentences.zh: 其以赦令蠲除以便於民，若逃移、戶絕不追者，景德中總六百八十二萬九千七百，皇祐中三十三萬八千四百五十七，治平中一千二百二十九萬八千七百。

translations.literal: That remitted by amnesty edicts for the people's convenience, such as flight and extinguished households not pursued: in Jingde totaling six million eight hundred twenty-nine thousand seven hundred; in Huangyou three hundred thirty-eight thousand four hundred fifty-seven; in Zhiping twelve million two hundred ninety-eight thousand seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty remissions—including write-offs for flight and extinct households—totaled 6,829,700 in Jingde, 338,457 in Huangyou, and 12,298,700 in Zhiping.

sentences.zh: 每歲以災害蠲除者，又不在是焉。

translations.literal: Each year's remissions due to disasters were again not included in these figures.
translations.idiomatic: Annual disaster remissions were not included in these totals.

sentences.zh: 神宗留意農賦，湖、廣之民舊歲輸丁米，大中祥符以後屢裁損，猶不均。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong paid attention to agricultural levies; the people of Huguang formerly paid poll rice annually; after Dazhong Xiangfu it was repeatedly cut and reduced, yet was still uneven.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong focused on agricultural taxation. Hu and Guang had long paid annual poll rice; though repeatedly cut since Dazhong Xiangfu, the burden remained uneven.

sentences.zh: 熙寧四年，乃遣屯田員外郎周之純往廣東相度均之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xining, Vice Director of Colonization Zhou Zhichun was dispatched to Guangdong to survey and equalize it.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 4, Vice Director of Colonization Zhou Zhichun was sent to Guangdong to survey and equalize the levy.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年，詔：諸路支移折稅，並具所行月日，上之中書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfeng, an edict: redirected delivery and converted tax on all circuits—all are to state the months and days of implementation and report to the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng 3, an edict required every circuit to report the dates of redirected deliveries and tax conversions to the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，熙寧八年，詔支移二稅於起納錢半歲諭民，使民宿辦，無倉卒勞費。

translations.literal: Initially, in the eighth year of Xining, an edict ordered that redirected delivery of the two taxes, half a year before collection began, inform the people, enabling lodging and preparation, without sudden labor and expense.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 8, an edict had required tax redirection plans for the two seasonal land taxes to be posted six months before collection so households could prepare without sudden hardship.

sentences.zh: 時有司往往緩期，故申約之。

translations.literal: At the time responsible offices often delayed the deadline; therefore the stipulation was reiterated.
translations.idiomatic: Because officials routinely missed deadlines, the requirement was restated in Yuanfeng 3.

sentences.zh: 州縣又或今民輸錢，謂之「折斛錢」，而糴賤頗用傷農。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties also sometimes ordered the people to pay cash, calling it "commuted peck money," and state grain purchases at low prices often harmed farmers.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials also sometimes required cash payments called "commuted peck fees," while cheap state grain purchases often hurt farmers.

sentences.zh: 海南四州軍稅籍殘缺，吏多增損，輒移稅入他戶，代輸者類不能自明。

translations.literal: In the four prefectures and military commissions of Hainan, tax registers were incomplete; officials frequently added or subtracted entries and shifted tax obligations onto other households; those who paid on others' behalf usually could not prove their case.
translations.idiomatic: Tax registers in Hainan's four prefectures and military commissions were incomplete. Officials routinely inflated or cut entries and shifted obligations onto other households, leaving substitute payers unable to clear their names.

sentences.zh: 瓊州、昌化軍丁稅米，歲移輸朱崖軍，道遠，民以為苦。

translations.literal: Ding-tax rice from Qiong Prefecture and Changhua Military Commission was annually redirected for delivery to Zhuyai Military Commission; the route was far, and the people found it onerous.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the ding-tax rice owed by Qiong Prefecture and Changhua Military Commission had to be shipped to distant Zhuyai Military Commission—a burden the people bitterly resented.

sentences.zh: 至是，用體量安撫朱初平等議，根括四州軍稅賦舊額，存其正數；

translations.literal: At this time, adopting the proposals of investigation-and-appeasement commissioner Zhu Chuping and others, they traced back the old tax quotas of the four prefectures and military commissions and kept only the correct figures;
translations.idiomatic: At this point the court adopted the recommendations of investigation commissioner Zhu Chuping and others, auditing the four prefectures' and military commissions' old tax quotas and retaining only the legitimate amounts;

sentences.zh: 二州丁稅米止令輸錢於朱崖自糴以便民。

translations.literal: For the two prefectures' ding-tax rice, they only required payment of cash at Zhuyai for local purchase, to ease matters for the people.
