translations.idiomatic: for the two prefectures' ding-tax rice they required only cash payment at Zhuyai, where grain could be purchased locally, to spare the people further hardship.

sentences.zh: 權發遣三司戶部判官李琮根究逃絕稅役，江、浙所得逃戶凡四十萬一千三百有奇，為書上之。

translations.literal: Acting commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue Li Cong was dispatched to investigate tax and corvée evaders; in Jiang and Zhe circuits the escaped households found totaled more than 401,300; he memorialized this in a report.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cong, acting commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue, was sent to investigate tax and corvée evasion. In the Jiang and Zhe circuits he found more than 401,300 escaped households and reported the figures in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 明年，除琮淮南轉運副使。

translations.literal: The next year, Cong was appointed vice transport commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Cong was appointed vice transport commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 兩路凡得逃絕、詭名挾佃、簿籍不載並闕丁凡四十七萬五千九百有奇，正稅並積負凡九十二萬二千二百貫、石、匹、兩有奇。

translations.literal: In the two circuits those found in categories of total escape, false names with tenant fraud, unregistered in ledgers, and missing ding totaled more than 475,900; regular taxes plus accumulated arrears totaled more than 922,200 strings, shi, bolts, and taels combined.
translations.idiomatic: Across both circuits he recovered more than 475,900 cases of total evasion, false names tied to tenant fraud, unregistered households, and missing adult males, along with more than 922,200 units of regular taxes and accumulated arrears in strings, shi, bolts, and taels.

sentences.zh: 琮蓋用貫石萬數立賞，以誘所委之吏，增加浩大，三路之民，大被其害。

translations.literal: Cong had set rewards in tens of thousands of strings and shi to entice the subordinates assigned to him; the additions were enormous, and the people of the three circuits suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Cong had offered rewards reckoned in tens of thousands of strings and shi to bait the officials under him, and the resulting increases were so vast that the people of all three circuits suffered heavily.

sentences.zh: 而唐州亦增民賦，人情騷然。

translations.literal: Tang Prefecture also increased the people's levies, and popular sentiment grew restless.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Prefecture raised levies as well, and public unrest spread.

sentences.zh: 六年，御史翟思言：「始，趙尚寬為唐守，勸民墾田，高賦繼之，流民自占者眾，凡百畝起稅四畝而已。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Censor Zhai Si said: "At first, when Zhao Shangkuan was prefect of Tang, he encouraged the people to open farmland; light levies followed; many refugees claimed land for themselves; only four mu per hundred mu were taxed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Censor Zhai Si said: "When Zhao Shangkuan was prefect of Tang, he encouraged reclamation and kept taxes light. Many refugees settled on their own land, and only four mu in every hundred were taxed.

sentences.zh: 稅輕而民樂輸，境內殆無曠土。

translations.literal: Taxes were light and the people were willing to pay; within the jurisdiction there was hardly any idle land.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were low and people paid willingly, until almost no land within the prefecture lay fallow.

sentences.zh: 近聞轉運司辟土百畝增至二十畝，恐其勢再致轉徙。

translations.literal: Recently it is heard that the transport commissioner has raised the taxed land on opened fields from four mu per hundred to twenty mu; I fear this will again cause migration.
translations.idiomatic: I now hear the transport commissioner has raised the taxable quota on newly opened land from four mu per hundred to twenty, and I fear this will drive people to flee again.

sentences.zh: 望戒飭使者，量加以寬民。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will admonish the commissioners and adjust the policy to ease the people.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty warn the commissioners and adjust the burden to give the people relief.

sentences.zh: 」帝每遇水旱，輒輕馳賦租；

translations.literal: Closing quotation. The Emperor, whenever encountering flood or drought, promptly remitted or deferred land taxes;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, whenever flood or drought struck, promptly remitted or deferred land taxes;

sentences.zh: 或因赦宥，又蠲放、倚閣未嘗絕；

translations.literal: or through amnesties granted remissions and deferred installments without interruption;
translations.idiomatic: and through amnesties granted remissions and payment deferrals almost without pause;

sentences.zh: 賦輸遠方不均，皆遣使按之，率以為常。

translations.literal: Uneven tax delivery to distant regions—envoys were always dispatched to investigate, and this became routine.
translations.idiomatic: whenever tax deliveries to distant regions fell unevenly, the court sent investigators—a practice that became routine.

sentences.zh: 哲宗嗣位，宣仁太后同聽政，務行裕民之政，凡民有負，多所寬減。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong succeeded, Empress Dowager Xuanren co-ruled and pursued policies to enrich the people; wherever the people owed arrears, there were many reductions.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong succeeded, Empress Dowager Xuanren shared power and pursued policies to ease the people's burden, granting wide reductions wherever arrears existed.

sentences.zh: 患天下積欠名目煩多，法令不一，王岩叟為開封，請隨等第立貫百為催法。

translations.literal: Concerned that accumulated arrears nationwide had too many categories and inconsistent regulations, Wang Yansou as Kaifeng prefect requested establishing a collection method by grade at one hundred strings per unit.
translations.idiomatic: Because accumulated arrears nationwide had grown tangled in category and law, Wang Yansou, prefect of Kaifeng, proposed a collection schedule by household grade in units of one hundred strings.

sentences.zh: 兗州鄒令張文仲議其不便，遂令十分為率，歲隨夏秋料帶納一分，是為五年十料之法。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenzong, magistrate of Zou in Yanzhou, argued it was impractical; so it was ordered that the rate be one-tenth, each year one-tenth of the summer and autumn quotas to be paid together—this was the ten-installment-over-five-years method.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenzong, magistrate of Zou in Yanzhou, argued that plan was unworkable, so the court set a one-tenth rate, allowing one-tenth of each summer and autumn quota to be paid annually—the ten-installment-over-five-years method.

sentences.zh: 陝西轉運使呂太忠令農戶支移，鬥輸腳錢十八。

translations.literal: Shaanxi transport commissioner Lü Taizhong ordered farming households on redirected delivery to pay eighteen cash per dou in transport fees.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi transport commissioner Lü Taizhong required farming households subject to branch transfer to pay eighteen cash per dou in transport fees.

sentences.zh: 御史劾之，下提刑司體量，均其輕重之等。

translations.literal: Censors impeached him; the case was sent to the judicial-intendancy circuit commission for investigation, to equalize the grades of lighter and heavier burdens.
translations.idiomatic: Censors impeached him, and the case was referred to the judicial-intendancy commission to investigate and equalize the lighter and heavier grades of burden.

sentences.zh: 以稅賦戶籍在第一等、第二等者支移三百里，三等、四等者二百里，五等一百里。

translations.literal: According to tax household registers, first- and second-grade households redirected delivery three hundred li; third- and fourth-grade two hundred li; fifth-grade one hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: By tax household grade, first- and second-grade households were redirected up to three hundred li, third- and fourth-grade up to two hundred li, and fifth-grade up to one hundred li.

sentences.zh: 不願支移而願輸道里腳價者，亦酌度分為三等，以從其便。

translations.literal: Those unwilling to redirect delivery but willing to pay route transport fees were also apportioned into three grades as appropriate, to suit their convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Those who preferred paying route transport fees instead of redirecting goods were likewise divided into three grades as appropriate, according to convenience.

sentences.zh: 河東助軍糧草，支移毋得逾三百里。

translations.literal: For Hedong military grain and fodder support, redirected delivery must not exceed three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: For Hedong grain and fodder supporting the army, branch transfer could not exceed three hundred li.

sentences.zh: 災傷五分以上者免折變，折變皆循舊法。

translations.literal: Where disaster damage exceeded five-tenths, commutation was exempted; all commutation followed the old law.
translations.idiomatic: Commutation was waived where crop loss exceeded fifty percent; otherwise commutation followed the old rules.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，嘗詔郡縣貨物用足錢、省陌不等，折變宜用中等。

translations.literal: In Shaosheng, an edict once ordered that when prefectures and counties used full cash and reduced-percent cash unequally for goods, commutation should use the middle rate.
translations.idiomatic: During Shaosheng an edict once ruled that where prefectures and counties used full cash and reduced-percent cash inconsistently in valuing goods, commutation should use the middle rate.

sentences.zh: 俄以所在時估實值多寡不齊，難概立法，命仍舊焉。

translations.literal: Soon because local current appraisals of actual value varied and uniform legislation was difficult, they were ordered to follow former practice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, because local market appraisals varied too widely for a uniform law, the court ordered the old practice restored.

sentences.zh: 言者謂：「欲民不流，不若多積穀；

translations.literal: Memorialists said: "If one wishes the people not to migrate, it is better to store much grain;
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists argued: "To keep people from fleeing, the state should stockpile grain;

sentences.zh: 欲多積穀，不若推行折納糶糴之法。

translations.literal: if one wishes to store much grain, it is better to implement the method of commuted payment and state grain sale and purchase.
translations.idiomatic: and to stockpile grain, it should expand commuted payment together with state grain purchase and release.

sentences.zh: 今常平雖有折納之法，止用中價，故民不樂輸。

translations.literal: Now although the Ever-Normal Granaries have a commuted-payment method, they use only the middle price, so the people are unwilling to deliver.
translations.idiomatic: The Ever-Normal Granaries already allow commuted payment, but because only the middle price is used, people are reluctant to pay in kind.

sentences.zh: 若依和糴以實價折之，則無損於民。」

translations.literal: If, following equitable purchase, conversion were made at actual price, then there would be no harm to the people."
translations.idiomatic: If commutation followed equitable purchase at actual market price, the people would not be harmed."

sentences.zh: 崇寧二年，諸路歲稔，遂行增價折納之法，支移、折變、科率、配買，皆以熙寧法從事，民以穀菽、物帛輸積負零稅者聽之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongning, all circuits had good harvests; the increased-price commuted-payment method was then implemented; branch transfer, commutation, assessed extractions, and assigned purchases all followed Xining law; the people were permitted to pay accumulated arrears and fractional taxes in grain, beans, and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning 2, after a good harvest across the circuits, the court imposed premium commuted payment and restored branch transfer, commutation, assessed extractions, and assigned purchases under the Xining rules, allowing arrears and fractional taxes to be paid in grain, beans, or cloth.

sentences.zh: 大觀二年詔：「天下租賦科撥支折，當先富後貧，自近及遠。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daguan, an edict said: "Nationwide rent and levies, assessed allocations, branch transfers, and conversions should put the wealthy before the poor and proceed from near to far.
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan 2 an edict declared: "Nationwide rent, levies, allocations, branch transfers, and conversions must burden the wealthy before the poor and proceed from near to far.

sentences.zh: 乃者漕臣失職，有不均之患，民或受害，其定為令。

translations.literal: Recently transport officials failed in duty, there was the affliction of inequality, and the people sometimes suffered harm; let this be fixed as statute.
translations.idiomatic: Transport officials have lately failed in duty, causing unequal burdens and harming the people. Let this be established as law.

sentences.zh: 支移本以便邊餉，內郡罕用焉。

translations.literal: Branch transfer was originally to facilitate frontier provisions; inner circuits rarely used it.
translations.idiomatic: Branch transfer had originally served frontier supply; interior circuits seldom used it.

sentences.zh: 間有移用，則任民以所費多寡自擇，故或輸本色於支移之地，或輸腳費於所居之邑。

translations.literal: When it was occasionally applied, the people were allowed to choose according to how much expense was involved; thus some delivered goods in kind at the branch-transfer destination, or paid transport fees in the town where they lived.
translations.idiomatic: When it was applied, people could choose according to cost: some delivered goods in kind at the transfer point, others paid transport fees in their home district.

sentences.zh: 而折變之法，以納月初旬估中價準折，仍視歲之豐歉，以定物之低昂，俾官吏毋得私其輕重。

translations.literal: As for the method of commutation, the middle price appraised in the first ten days of the payment month was taken as the standard for conversion; still looking to the year's abundance or scarcity to fix goods high or low, so that officials could not privately manipulate lighter or heavier valuation.
translations.idiomatic: Commutation was to be calculated from the middle market price appraised in the first ten days of the payment month, adjusted for the year's harvest to set high or low values so officials could not manipulate the rate.

sentences.zh: 」七月，詔曰：「比聞慢吏廢期，凡輸官之物，違期促限，蠶者未絲，農者未獲，追胥旁午，民無所措。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. In the seventh month, an edict said: "Recently it is heard that negligent officials missed deadlines; for all goods delivered to government, deadlines were violated and limits pressed; silkworm raisers had not yet reeled silk, farmers had not yet harvested; tax runners pressed from all sides, and the people had nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month an edict said: "We hear negligent officials are forcing deadlines before silkworms are reeled or crops harvested, with tax runners pressing people on every side until they have nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 自今前期督輸者，加一等坐之；

translations.literal: From now on, those who press delivery ahead of schedule shall be punished one grade higher;
translations.idiomatic: From now on, officials who demand early payment shall be punished one grade more severely;

sentences.zh: 致民逃徙者，論更加等。

translations.literal: those who cause the people to flee and migrate shall be judged with an additional grade added.
translations.idiomatic: and those who drive people to flee shall be punished still more severely.

sentences.zh: 」舊凡以赦令蠲賦，雖多不過三分。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. Formerly, whenever levies were remitted by amnesty edict, even at most it did not exceed three-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, amnesty remissions of levies rarely exceeded thirty percent.

sentences.zh: 四年，乃詔：天下逋賦，五年外戶口不存者，悉蠲之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict then ordered: Arrears nationwide, where after five years the household no longer existed, were all remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year an edict remitted all arrears more than five years old where the household no longer existed.

sentences.zh: 京西舊不支移，崇寧中，將漕者忽令民曰：「支移所宜同，今特免；

translations.literal: Jingxi Circuit formerly had no branch transfer; in Chongning, transport officials suddenly told the people: "Branch transfer should be the same everywhere; now it is specially exempted;
translations.idiomatic: Jingxi Circuit had never used branch transfer, but in Chongning transport officials suddenly told the people: "Branch transfer should be uniform everywhere, so you are now exempt;

sentences.zh: 若地裏腳費，則宜輸。

translations.literal: but overland transport fees should still be paid."
translations.idiomatic: but overland transport fees must still be paid."

sentences.zh: 」自是歲以為常。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. From then on this became annual routine.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter this became an annual charge.

sentences.zh: 腳費，鬥為錢五十六，比元豐即當正稅之數，而反覆紐折，數倍於昔。

translations.literal: Transport fees were fifty-six cash per dou; compared with Yuanfeng this already equaled the amount of regular tax, yet through repeated twisted conversions they became several times what they had been.
translations.idiomatic: Transport fees reached fifty-six cash per dou—under Yuanfeng already equal to the regular tax—yet repeated commutation drove them several times higher.

sentences.zh: 民至鬻牛易產猶不能繼，轉運司乃用是以取辦理之譽，言者極論其害。

translations.literal: The people reached the point of selling oxen and exchanging property yet still could not keep up; the transport commission then used this to win credit for efficient collection, and memorialists strongly argued its harm.
translations.idiomatic: People sold oxen and property and still could not keep up, while transport commissioners claimed credit for efficient collection until critics denounced the abuse at length.

sentences.zh: 政和元年，遂詔應支移而所輸地裏腳錢不及鬥者，免之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenghe, an edict then remitted overland transport fees where branch transfer applied but the fee paid was less than one dou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 1 an edict exempted overland transport fees owed under branch transfer when the amount was less than one dou.

sentences.zh: 尋詔五等戶稅不及鬥者，支移皆免。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered that fifth-grade households whose tax was less than one dou were entirely exempt from branch transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Soon another edict exempted all fifth-grade households whose tax fell below one dou from branch transfer entirely.

sentences.zh: 時天下戶口類多不實，雖嘗立法比較鉤考，歲終會其數，按籍隱括脫漏，定賞罰之格，然蔡攸等計德、霸二州戶口之數，率三戶四口，則戶版訛隱，不待校而知。

translations.literal: At the time household registers nationwide were mostly inaccurate; although laws were once made for comparative audit and verification, at year's end totals were reconciled, registers searched for concealed omissions, and reward-and-punishment standards fixed—yet when Cai You and others calculated household numbers in De and Ba prefectures, the rate was three households to four persons; then register falsification and concealment needed no verification to be known.
translations.idiomatic: Household registers nationwide were largely false. Though the court had instituted comparative audits, year-end reconciliations, and rewards and punishments for concealed omissions, when Cai You and others calculated De and Ba prefectures at barely three households for every four persons, the fraud needed no audit to be obvious.

sentences.zh: 乃詔諸路凡奏戶口，令提刑司及提舉常平司參考保奏。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered that on all circuits, whenever household numbers were memorialized, the judicial-intendancy and Ever-Normal Granary circuit commissions were to examine and guarantee the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then required judicial-intendancy and Ever-Normal Granary commissions on every circuit to review and certify household reports.

sentences.zh: 而終莫能拯其弊，故租稅亦不得而均焉。

translations.literal: Yet in the end they could not rescue this abuse, so rent and taxes likewise could not be made equal.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the abuse was never corrected, and rent and taxes could not be equalized.

sentences.zh: 是時，內外之費浸以不給，中官楊戩主後苑作，有言汝州地可為稻田者，因用其言，置務掌之，號「稻田務』。

translations.literal: At this time, internal and external expenses gradually became insufficient; palace eunuch Yang Jian supervised rear-garden construction; someone said land in Ruzhou could serve as rice fields; adopting this advice, an office was established to manage it, called the "Rice Field Office."
translations.idiomatic: By then internal and external expenses were outrunning revenue. Palace eunuch Yang Jian, who oversaw imperial garden works, heard that land in Ruzhou could be turned into rice paddies; the court acted on the suggestion and established the Rice Field Office.

sentences.zh: 復行於府畿，易名公田。

translations.literal: It was extended to the capital region and renamed Public Fields.
translations.idiomatic: The scheme spread to the capital region and was renamed Public Fields.

sentences.zh: 南暨襄、唐，西及澠池，北逾大河，民田有溢於初券步畝者，輒使輸公田錢。

translations.literal: South reaching Xiang and Tang, west to Mianchi, north beyond the Great River, wherever civilian fields exceeded the paces and mu of the original deed, they were immediately made to pay Public Field money.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiang and Tang in the south to Mianchi in the west and beyond the Yellow River in the north, any farmland exceeding the area on the original deed was charged Public Field fees.

sentences.zh: 政和末，又置營繕所，亦為公田。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenghe, a Construction Office was also established, likewise as Public Fields.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhenghe the court also established a Construction Office under the same Public Fields scheme.

sentences.zh: 久之，後苑、營繕所公田皆並於西城所，盡山東、河朔天荒逃田與河堤退灘租稅舉入焉，皆內侍主其事。

translations.literal: After long time, Public Fields of the rear garden and Construction Office were all merged into the Western Capital Office; all wilderness and abandoned fields of Shandong and Hebei and rent taxes on river-bank retreat sands were swept into it; all were managed by palace eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: In time the rear-garden and construction Public Fields were merged into the Western Capital Office, which absorbed wilderness and abandoned land across Shandong and Hebei together with rent from river-bank retreat lands—all under palace eunuch control.

sentences.zh: 所括為田三萬四千三百餘頃，民輸公田錢外，正稅不復能輸。

translations.literal: Land seized totaled more than 34,300 qing; beyond paying Public Field money, the people could no longer deliver regular taxes.
translations.idiomatic: More than 34,300 qing were seized, and beyond Public Field fees people could no longer pay their regular taxes.

sentences.zh: 重和元年，獻言者曰：「物有豐匱，價有低昂，估豐賤之物，俾民輸送，折價既賤，輸官必多，則公私之利也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chonghe, a memorialist said: "Goods have abundance and scarcity, prices have low and high; appraising abundant and cheap goods and making the people deliver them, since converted price is cheap, what is delivered to government must be much—then there is benefit to public and private alike.
translations.idiomatic: In Chonghe 1 a memorialist argued: "When goods are plentiful and cheap, commutation at low appraisal lets people deliver more to the state at little cost—a benefit to both public and private interests.

sentences.zh: 而州縣之吏，但計一方所乏，不計物之有無，責民所無，其費無量。

translations.literal: Yet prefecture and county officials only calculated what one region lacked, not whether the goods existed; they demanded from the people what they did not have—the cost was boundless.
translations.idiomatic: But prefecture and county officials looked only at local shortages, not at what people actually possessed, demanding goods they did not have at limitless cost.

sentences.zh: 至於支移，徙豐就歉，理則宜然。

translations.literal: As for branch transfer, shifting from abundance to scarcity was reasonable in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Branch transfer, in principle, should move goods from abundance to scarcity.

sentences.zh: 豪民賕吏，故徙歉以就豐，齎挾輕貨，以賤價輸官，其利自倍；

translations.literal: Powerful households and bribed officials deliberately shifted from scarcity toward abundance, carrying light goods and delivering to government at cheap price—their profit doubled of itself;
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy families and bribed officials reversed the flow from scarcity to abundance, bringing lightweight goods and paying at low appraisal to double their profit;

sentences.zh: 而貧下戶各免支移，估值既高，更益腳費，視富戶反重。

translations.literal: while poor households were each exempt from branch transfer; since appraisal was high, transport fees were further increased, so compared with wealthy households their burden was instead heavier.
translations.idiomatic: while poor households, exempt from branch transfer, faced high appraisals plus transport fees and thus paid more than the wealthy.

sentences.zh: 因之逋負，困於追胥。

translations.literal: Because of this they fell into arrears and were distressed by tax runners.
translations.idiomatic: They fell into arrears and were hounded by tax collectors.

sentences.zh: 」詔申戒焉。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. An edict admonished accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued a warning edict.

sentences.zh: 宣和初，州縣主吏催科失職，逋租數廣，令轉運司察守貳勤惰，聽專達於內侍省。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanhe, chief clerks of prefectures and counties failed in tax collection; arrears of rent were extensive; transport commissioners were ordered to inspect prefects and vice-prefects for diligence or laziness, and permitted to report directly to the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuanhe, chief clerks failed at tax collection and rent arrears mounted. Transport commissioners were ordered to inspect prefects and vice-prefects for diligence and report directly to the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 浙西逃田、天荒、草田、葑茭蕩、湖濼退灘等地，皆計籍召佃立租，以供應奉。

translations.literal: In western Zhejiang, abandoned fields, wilderness, grassland, reed and aquatic plots, lake and marsh retreat sands and the like—all were entered in registers, tenants summoned, and rent established, to supply imperial tribute expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In western Zhejiang, abandoned fields, wilderness, grassland, reed flats, and lake retreat lands were all registered, leased out, and taxed to fund imperial tribute expenses.

sentences.zh: 置局命官，有「措置水利農田」之名，部使者且自督御前租課。

translations.literal: An office was established and officials appointed under the name "Arrangements for Waterworks and Farmland"; circuit commissioners themselves also supervised imperial-front rent and levies.
translations.idiomatic: The court established an office called "Arrangements for Waterworks and Farmland" and even circuit commissioners personally oversaw imperial-front rent and levies.

sentences.zh: 三年，言者論西蜀折科之弊，其略謂：「西蜀初稅錢三百折絹一匹，草十圍計錢二十。

translations.literal: In the third year, memorialists discussed the abuses of commuted assessment in western Shu; the summary said: "Western Shu originally taxed three hundred cash commuted to one bolt of silk; ten bundles of fodder counted as twenty cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year critics described commutation abuses in western Shu: "Originally three hundred cash in tax commuted to one bolt of silk, and ten bundles of fodder counted as twenty cash.

sentences.zh: 今本路絹不用本色，匹折草百五十圍，圍估錢百五十，稅錢三百輸至二十三千。

translations.literal: Now in this circuit silk is not taken in kind; each bolt is commuted to one hundred fifty bundles of fodder; each bundle appraised at one hundred fifty cash; three hundred cash in tax rises to payment of twenty-three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Now the circuit no longer accepts silk in kind. Each bolt commutes to 150 bundles of fodder at 150 cash per bundle, turning a 300-cash tax into 23,000 cash owed.

sentences.zh: 東蜀如之。

translations.literal: Eastern Shu was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Shu fared no better.

sentences.zh: 仍支移新邊，謂之遠倉，民破產者眾。

translations.literal: Still branch transfer was to the new frontier, called distant granaries; many people were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Goods were still redirected to new frontier granaries, and many people were ruined.

sentences.zh: 」七年，言者又論：「非法折變，既以絹折錢，又以錢折麥。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. In the seventh year, memorialists again argued: "Illegal commutation—first converting silk to cash, then converting cash to wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year critics added: "Through illegal commutation, silk was converted to cash and cash to wheat.

sentences.zh: 以絹較錢，錢倍於絹；

translations.literal: Comparing cash to silk, cash doubled silk;
translations.idiomatic: Cash valued against silk doubled the silk burden;

sentences.zh: 以錢較麥，麥倍於錢。

translations.literal: comparing wheat to cash, wheat doubled cash.
translations.idiomatic: wheat valued against cash doubled the cash burden.

sentences.zh: 展轉增加，民無所訴。」

translations.literal: Turning and increasing in succession, the people had nowhere to appeal."
translations.idiomatic: Each conversion piled on the last, leaving people no recourse."

sentences.zh: 唐、鄧、襄，汝等州，自治平後，開墾歲增，然未定稅額。

translations.literal: Tang, Deng, Xiang, Ru and other prefectures, since Zhiping, yearly increased in opened reclamation, yet fixed tax quotas were not established.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhiping, Tang, Deng, Xiang, Ru, and other prefectures had steadily expanded reclamation, but no fixed tax quotas had been set.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，以所墾新田差為五等輸稅，元祐元年罷之。

translations.literal: In Yuanfeng, newly reclaimed fields were graded into five classes for tax payment; in the first year of Yuanyou this was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanfeng newly reclaimed land was taxed in five grades; Yuanyou 1 abolished the rule.

sentences.zh: 大觀三年，用轉運副使張徽言之請，復元豐舊制，俄又以訴者而罷。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daguan, adopting the request of vice transport commissioner Zhang Huizhi, the Yuanfeng old system was restored; soon it was again abolished because of petitioners.
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan 3, at the request of vice transport commissioner Zhang Huizhi, the Yuanfeng system was restored, only to be abolished again after protests.

sentences.zh: 政和三年，轉運使王璹復言官失租賦，詔依元豐法，第折以見錢，凡得三十萬緡。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe, transport commissioner Wang Shan again said the government was losing rent and levies; an edict ordered following Yuanfeng law, only commuted to current cash; in all three hundred thousand strings were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 3 transport commissioner Wang Shan again reported lost rent and levies. The court restored the Yuanfeng rule, commuted only to current cash, and collected 300,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 欽宗立，詔蠲焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Qinzong succeeded, an edict remitted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Qinzong succeeded, an edict remitted the levy.

sentences.zh: 舊稅租加耗，轉運司有拋樁明耗，州縣有暗樁暗耗之名，諸倉場受納，又令民輸頭子錢。

translations.literal: Formerly rent and tax had added wastage; transport commissioners had declared markup wastage; prefectures and counties had hidden markup wastage; at all granary yards upon receipt the people were also made to pay surcharge fees.
translations.idiomatic: Rent and tax had long carried added wastage allowances—declared markup at the transport level, hidden markup at the prefecture and county level, and surcharge fees at every granary upon receipt.

sentences.zh: 熙寧以後，給納並收，其數益增焉，至是悉罷。

translations.literal: After Xining, delivery and payment were all collected together; the amounts increasingly grew; at this time all were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: After Xining these fees were collected together at delivery and steadily increased until they were all abolished at this time.

sentences.zh: 高宗建炎元年五月庚寅，詔二稅並依舊法，凡百姓欠租、閣賦及應天府夏稅，悉蠲之。

translations.literal: On gengyin day of the fifth month of the first year of Jianyan under Gaozong, an edict ordered both taxes to follow the old law; all common people's arrears of rent, deferred levies, and summer tax of Yingtian Prefecture were all remitted.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day in the fifth month of Jianyan 1, Gaozong ordered both taxes restored to the old rules and remitted all rent arrears, deferred levies, and Yingtian Prefecture's summer tax.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔被虜之家蠲夏秋租稅及科配。

translations.literal: On gengzi day, an edict remitted summer and autumn rent and taxes and apportioned surcharges for households taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day an edict remitted summer and autumn taxes and apportioned surcharges for families taken captive.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年五月詔：「民力久困，州縣因緣為奸，今頒式諸路，凡因軍期不得已而貸於民者，並許計所用之多寡，度物力之輕重，依式開具，使民通知，毋得過數科率。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Shaoxing, an edict said: "The people's strength has long been exhausted; prefectures and counties seize opportunities for fraud; now a form is promulgated to all circuits: wherever because of military deadlines there is no choice but to borrow from the people, all are permitted to calculate amount used, assess light or heavy of material strength, set forth according to form, let the people be informed, and not exceed quota in assessed extraction.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Shaoxing 1 an edict said: "The people are exhausted and local officials abuse their power. A standard form is now sent to every circuit: any levy forced on the people for military deadlines must list actual costs and local capacity, inform the public, and never exceed authorized quotas.

sentences.zh: 」八月，減大觀稅額三分之一。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. In the eighth month, Daguan tax quotas were reduced by one-third.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Daguan-era tax quotas were cut by one-third.

sentences.zh: 十有一月，言者論：「浙西科斂之害，農末殆不聊生。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, memorialists argued: "The harm of forced extraction in western Zhejiang—farmers and merchants can scarcely survive.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month critics said: "Forced extractions in western Zhejiang have left farmers and merchants barely able to live.

sentences.zh: 鬻田而償，則無受者；

translations.literal: If they sold fields to pay, then there were none who would accept;
translations.idiomatic: If they sold land to pay, no one would buy;

sentences.zh: 棄之而遁，則質其妻孥。

translations.literal: If they abandoned fields and fled, then their wives and children were pledged.
translations.idiomatic: If they abandoned everything and fled, creditors seized their wives and children.

sentences.zh: 上下相蒙，民無所措手足。

translations.literal: Superiors and subordinates deceived one another; the people had nowhere to place hands or feet.
translations.idiomatic: Officials deceived one another while the people had nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 利歸貪吏，而怨歸陛下。

translations.literal: Profit went to greedy officials, while resentment fell on Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy officials kept the profit while public resentment fell on Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 願重科斂之罪，嚴貪墨之刑。

translations.literal: I wish that the crime of forced extraction be made heavy and the punishment of corruption be made strict.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that forced extraction be punished severely and corruption dealt with harshly.

sentences.zh: 」詔漕司究實以聞。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. An edict ordered transport offices to investigate the facts and report.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered transport offices to investigate and report.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，知紹興府陳汝錫違詔科率，謫漳州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Chen Ruxi, prefect of Shaoxing, violated the edict in assessed extraction and was demoted to Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Chen Ruxi, prefect of Shaoxing, was demoted to Zhangzhou for unauthorized extractions.

sentences.zh: 四月，建盜範汝為平，詔蠲本路今年二稅及夏科役錢。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the bandit Fan Ruwei in Jian was pacified; an edict remitted this year's both taxes and summer corvée money for this circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, after the bandit Fan Ruwei in Jian was suppressed, an edict remitted the circuit's two taxes and summer corvée fees for the year.

sentences.zh: 既而手詔：「訪聞州縣以為著令不過三分，甚非所以稱朕惠恤之意，可以赦並免。

translations.literal: Soon afterward an imperial hand edict said: "In inquiry it is heard that prefectures and counties think the statute allows no more than three-tenths remission; this greatly fails to match my intent to show favor and care; through amnesty all may be exempted together.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong then wrote by hand: "I hear local officials limit remissions to thirty percent as if that were the law. That does not reflect my intent to show mercy. Let all be remitted through amnesty.

sentences.zh: 」十有一月，焚州縣已蠲稅薄，示民以不疑也。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. In the eleventh month, remitted tax ledgers of prefectures and counties were burned, to show the people there was no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the court burned local remission ledgers so the people would trust the relief.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，詔諸路轉運司以增收租數上戶部，課賞罰。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year, an edict ordered transport offices of all circuits to report increased rent figures to the Ministry of Revenue and assess rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year an edict ordered every circuit's transport office to report increased rent collections to the Ministry of Revenue for reward or punishment.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，預借江、浙來年夏稅綢絹之半，盡令折米：兩浙綢絹各折七千，江南六千有半，每匹折米二石。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year, half of next year's summer-tax silk and satin from Jiang and Zhe was prepaid, all ordered converted to rice: Two-Zhe silk and satin each converted seven thousand, Jiangnan six thousand and a half, each bolt converted two shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the sixth year the court prepaid half of Jiang and Zhe's next-year summer silk tax and required all of it paid in rice: Two-Zhe silk and satin at seven thousand each, Jiangnan at six thousand five hundred, with each bolt reckoned at two shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 九月，右司諫王搢言：「諸寺院之多產者，類請求貴臣改為墳院，冀免科敷，則所科歸之下戶。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Right Remonstrance Bureau remonstrator Wang Jin said: "Monasteries with much property often request powerful officials to reclassify them as cemetery estates, hoping to escape assessed extractions, so the assessments fall on lower households.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wang Jin of the Right Remonstrance Bureau reported that wealthy monasteries often had patrons reclassify them as funerary cloisters to evade levies, shifting the burden onto poorer households.

sentences.zh: 」詔戶部申嚴禁之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. An edict ordered the Ministry of Revenue to issue strict prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the Ministry of Revenue to enforce a strict ban.

sentences.zh: 十有二月，詔淮西殘破州縣更免租稅二年。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, an edict remitted rent and tax for two more years in ruined prefectures and counties of Huai West.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month an edict granted two further years of rent and tax relief to devastated prefectures and counties in Huai West.

sentences.zh: 是月戊申，詔曰：「朕惟養兵之費，皆取於民，吾民甚苦；

translations.literal: On the wushen day of that month, an edict said: "I consider that the expense of maintaining troops is all taken from the people; my people suffer greatly;
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day that month Gaozong issued an edict: "The cost of keeping armies comes entirely from the people, and my people are sorely burdened;

sentences.zh: 而吏莫之恤，夤緣軍須，掊斂無藝，朕甚悼之。

translations.literal: yet officials do not care for them, riding on military needs to extort without limit; I grieve deeply over this.
translations.idiomatic: yet officials show no concern, using military supply as a pretext for limitless exactions. I am deeply grieved.

sentences.zh: 監司郡守，朕所委寄以惠養元元者也，今漫不加省，復何賴焉！

translations.literal: Intendants and prefects are those I entrust to nurture the common people; now they carelessly give no attention—on whom else can I rely!
translations.idiomatic: Intendants and prefects are the men I rely on to care for the people. If they pay no heed, whom can I trust?

sentences.zh: 其各勤乃職，察民之侵漁納賄者，按劾以聞。

translations.literal: Let each diligently perform his duty, investigate those who prey on the people and accept bribes, impeach and report.
translations.idiomatic: Let each of you perform your duties diligently, investigate officials who extort or take bribes, and report them for prosecution.

sentences.zh: 苟庇覆弗治，朕不汝貸。

translations.literal: If you shelter and fail to punish, I will not spare you.
translations.idiomatic: If you shield wrongdoers and fail to act, I will show you no mercy.

sentences.zh: 」是歲，兩浙轉運李迨取婺秀湖州、平江府歲計寬剩錢二十二萬八千緡有奇，依折帛錢限起發。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. That year, Two-Zhe transport commissioner Li Dai took surplus year-plan funds of 228,000-odd strings from Wuzhou, Xiuzhou, Huzhou, and Pingjiang Prefecture, dispatching them according to the deadline for converted-silk cash.
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Dai, transport commissioner for Two Zhe, drew more than 228,000 strings in surplus annual funds from Wuzhou, Xiuzhou, Huzhou, and Pingjiang and forwarded them on the schedule for converted-silk payments.

sentences.zh: 自是以為例。

translations.literal: From this it became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: This thereafter became standard practice.

sentences.zh: 七年三月，詔：駐蹕及所過州縣欠紹興五年以前稅賦，並蠲之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year, an edict: tax and tribute arrears before the fifth year of Shaoxing in prefectures where the court stayed or passed through were all remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year an edict remitted all tax arrears before Shaoxing 5 in counties and prefectures where the court had sojourned or traveled.

sentences.zh: 七月，詔：新復州軍請佃官田，輸租外免輸正稅。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, an edict: in newly recovered prefectures and armies, tenants of government land were exempt from paying regular tax beyond rent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month an edict exempted tenants of government land in newly recovered prefectures and garrisons from paying regular land tax in addition to rent.

translations.literal: Opening bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note follows.

sentences.zh: （己田謂之稅，佃田謂之租，舊不並納，劉豫嘗並取之，至是，乃從舊法。）〉

translations.literal: (One's own land was called tax; tenanted land was called rent. Formerly these were not collected together. Liu Yu once collected both. At this time the old law was restored.) Closing bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Note: tax applied to owned land and rent to leased land; they had not been collected together until Liu Yu combined them. The old rule was now restored.

sentences.zh: 九年，蠲新復州軍稅租及土貢、大禮銀絹三年，差徭五年。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, remitted tax and rent, local tribute, and grand-ceremony silver and silk for three years in newly recovered prefectures and armies, and corvée for five years.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year newly recovered prefectures and garrisons received three years' relief from land tax, rent, local tribute, and grand-ceremony silver and silk, and five years' relief from corvée.

sentences.zh: 初，劉豫之僭，凡民間蔬圃皆令三季輸稅。

translations.literal: Initially, when Liu Yu usurped power, all private vegetable gardens were made to pay tax for three seasons.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu first seized power he had even private vegetable plots taxed three seasons a year.

sentences.zh: 宣諭官方庭實言其不便，起居舍人程克俊言：「河南父老苦豫煩苛久矣，賦斂及於絮縷，割剝至於果蔬。

translations.literal: Remonstration commissioner Fang Tingshi reported the inconvenience; attendant scribe Cheng Kejun said: "The elders of Henan have long suffered from Yu's vexatious harshness; taxation reached even cotton thread, extraction extended even to fruits and vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstration commissioner Fang Tingshi reported the hardship, and attendant scribe Cheng Kejun said: "The people of Henan have long endured Liu Yu's oppressive levies, taxed down to scraps of cotton and stripped even of fruit and vegetables.

sentences.zh: 」於是詔新復州縣，取劉豫重斂之法焚之通衢。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. Thereupon an edict ordered newly recovered prefectures and counties to take Liu Yu's heavy-extraction regulations and burn them in public thoroughfares.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered newly recovered prefectures and counties to burn Liu Yu's harsh tax regulations in the public streets.

sentences.zh: 十三年，淮東宣撫使韓世忠請以賜田及私產自昔未輸之稅並歸之官，詔獎諭而可之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Huai East pacification commissioner Han Shizhong asked that unpaid taxes on granted lands and private property from former times all be surrendered to the state; an edict commended him and approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Han Shizhong, pacification commissioner of Huai East, offered to surrender all back taxes owed on his granted and private lands; the court praised and accepted his request.

sentences.zh: 初，神武右軍統製張俊乞蠲所置產凡和買、科敷，詔特從之。

translations.literal: Initially, Shenwu Right Army controller Zhang Jun requested remission of all equitable purchase and assessed extractions on his acquired property; an edict specially granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Jun, controller of the Shenwu Right Army, had asked exemption from equitable purchase and special levies on property he had acquired, and the court had granted it.

sentences.zh: 後，三省言：「國家兵革未息，用度至廣，陛下哀憫元元，俾士大夫及勳戚之家與編戶等敷，蓋欲寬民力，均有無。

translations.literal: Later, the Three Departments said: "The state has not ceased from warfare; expenses are very great. Your Majesty pities the common people and had scholar-officials and meritorious families share assessments equally with registered households, intending to ease the people's burden and equalize rich and poor.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Three Departments argued: "With war continuing and expenses vast, Your Majesty had officials and meritorious families share levies equally with common households to ease the people's burden and spread the cost fairly.

sentences.zh: 今俊獨得免，則當均在餘戶，是使民為俊代輸也。

translations.literal: Now Jun alone is exempted, so the equal burden must fall on remaining households—this makes the people pay in Jun's stead.
translations.idiomatic: If Zhang Jun alone is exempt, his share must fall on everyone else—making the people pay his taxes for him.

sentences.zh: 方今大將不止俊一人，使各援例求免，何以拒之？

translations.literal: At present great generals are not limited to Jun alone; if each invokes precedent to seek exemption, how can they be refused?
translations.idiomatic: There are many great generals besides Zhang Jun. If each cites his example, how can any refusal be made?

sentences.zh: 望收還前詔。

translations.literal: We hope the prior edict may be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the earlier edict be revoked.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 越數年間，俊復乞免歲輸和買絹，三省擬歲賜俊絹五千匹，庶免起例。

translations.literal: Several years later, Jun again asked exemption from yearly equitable-purchase silk delivery; the Three Departments proposed annually granting him five thousand bolts of silk, hoping to avoid setting a precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later Zhang Jun again sought exemption from his annual equitable-purchase silk quota. The Three Departments proposed granting him five thousand bolts of silk each year to avoid creating a precedent.

sentences.zh: 上以示俊，因諭之曰：「朕固不惜，但恐公議不可。

translations.literal: The emperor showed this to Jun and instructed him: "I personally do not begrudge it, but I fear public opinion would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed him the proposal and said: "I would not begrudge the silk, but I fear public opinion would not tolerate it.

sentences.zh: 」俊惶悚，力辭賜絹。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. Jun was fearful and declined the grant of silk emphatically.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, alarmed, firmly declined the grant.

translations.idiomatic: If county chao were lost or destroyed, the supervisor and retained copies were used to cancel the record;

sentences.zh: 若輒取戶鈔，或追驗於人戶者，科杖。」

translations.literal: if household chao were arbitrarily taken, or verification was pursued against the household, beating with the staff was imposed." Closing quotation.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，知池州黃子遊言：「青陽縣苗七八倍於諸縣，因南唐嘗以縣為宋齊丘食邑，畝輸三斗，後遂為額。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Huang Ziyou, prefect of Chizhou, said: "Qingyang County's seed tax is seven or eight times that of other counties, because Southern Tang once made the county Song Qiqiu's fief; three dou per mu was paid, and afterward this became the quota.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year Huang Ziyou, prefect of Chizhou, reported that Qingyang County's seed tax was seven or eight times higher than elsewhere because Southern Tang had made it Song Qiqiu's fief at three dou per mu, a rate that later became fixed.

sentences.zh: 」詔減苗稅二分有半，租米二分。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. An edict reduced seed tax by two and a half tenths and rent grain by two tenths.
translations.idiomatic: The court reduced the seed tax by twenty-five percent and rent grain by twenty percent.

sentences.zh: 是時，兩浙州縣合輸綿、綢、稅絹、茶絹、雜錢、米六色，皆以市價折錢，卻別科米麥，有畝輸四五斗者。

translations.literal: At this time Two-Zhe prefectures and counties together owed six categories—cotton, silk, tax silk, tea silk, miscellaneous cash, and grain—all converted to cash at market price, yet grain and wheat were separately assessed; some paid four or five dou per mu.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Two-Zhe prefectures and counties owed six kinds of dues—cotton, silk, tax silk, tea silk, miscellaneous cash, and grain—all commuted to cash at market rates, while grain and wheat were also assessed separately; some households paid four or five dou per mu.

sentences.zh: 京西括田，租加於舊。

translations.literal: In Jingxi, consolidated land caused rent to increase above former levels.
translations.idiomatic: In Jing West, land consolidation had raised rents above former levels.

sentences.zh: 湖南有土戶錢、折絁錢、醋息錢、曲引錢，名色不一。

translations.literal: In Hunan there were native-household cash, converted-ze cash, vinegar-interest cash, and yeast-levy cash—categories varied.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan had native-household fees, hemp conversion fees, vinegar-interest fees, and yeast-license fees under many different names.

sentences.zh: 荊南戶口十萬，寇亂以來，幾無人跡。

translations.literal: Jingnan had one hundred thousand registered households; since the bandit disorders, almost no human trace remained.
translations.idiomatic: Jingnan had once registered one hundred thousand households, but since the rebellions the region was nearly depopulated.

sentences.zh: 議者希朝廷意，謂流民已復，可使歲輸十二，頻歲復增，積逋至二十餘萬緡。

translations.literal: Deliberators expecting court favor said refugees had returned and annual payment of one hundred twenty thousand strings could be required; year after year it was again increased, accumulated arrears reaching over two hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Officials eager to please the court claimed refugees had returned and set an annual quota of 120,000 strings, then raised it year after year until arrears exceeded 200,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 曹泳為戶部侍郎，責償甚急。

translations.literal: Cao Yong as Vice Minister of Revenue pressed collection very urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yong, vice minister of revenue, pressed collection relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 蓋自檜再相，密諭諸路暗增民稅七八，故民力重困，餓死者眾，皆檜之為也。

translations.literal: From when Hui again became chief councilor, he secretly instructed all circuits to covertly increase people's taxes by seven or eight tenths, so the people's strength was heavily strained and many starved to death—all Hui's doing.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin Hui returned as chief councilor he had secretly ordered circuits to raise taxes by seventy or eighty percent, crushing the people and causing widespread starvation—all of it Qin Hui's work.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，先是，承議郎魯衝上書論郡邑之弊：「以臣前任宜興一縣言之，漕計合收窠名，有丁鹽、坊場課利錢，租地錢，租絲租紵錢，歲入不過一萬五千餘緡。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, earlier, Gentlemen for Court Discussion Lu Chong memorialized on the ills of prefectures and counties: "Taking my former post in Yixing County alone, the transport-plan receivables by category included ding-salt, workshop-course profits, rent-land cash, and rent-silk and rent-ramie cash—annual intake was no more than about fifteen thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year Gentlemen for Court Discussion Lu Chong had memorialized on local abuses: "In my former county of Yixing alone, transport-plan receipts under various categories—ding salt, workshop profits, rent-land fees, and rent-silk and rent-ramie fees—totaled barely fifteen thousand strings a year.

sentences.zh: 其發納之數，有大軍錢、上供錢、糴本錢、造船錢、軍器物料錢、天申節銀絹錢之類，歲支不啻三萬四千餘緡。

translations.literal: Disbursements included great-army cash, tribute-up cash, grain-purchase capital, shipbuilding cash, military-material cash, Tian Shen Festival silver and silk cash, and the like—annual outlay was no less than about thirty-four thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Yet disbursements—for the main army, tribute, grain purchases, shipbuilding, military supplies, Tian Shen Festival silver and silk, and the like—came to more than thirty-four thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 又有見任、寄居官請奉、過往官兵批券、與非泛州郡督索拖欠，略無虛日。

translations.literal: There were also salaries for incumbent and sojourning officials, travel vouchers for passing troops, and miscellaneous prefectural and county demands for arrears—hardly a day without them.
translations.idiomatic: On top of that came salaries for resident and sojourning officials, travel vouchers for passing troops, and miscellaneous prefectural and county demands for arrears—hardly a day passed without new exactions.

sentences.zh: 今之為令者，苟以寬恤為意，而拙於催科，旋踵以不職罷；

translations.literal: Today's magistrates, if they intend leniency but are poor at collection, are soon dismissed for incompetence;
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates who tried to be lenient but were poor collectors were quickly removed for incompetence;

sentences.zh: 能迎合上司，慘刻聚斂，則以稱職聞。

translations.literal: those who can please superiors through cruel extraction are reported as performing well.
translations.idiomatic: those who pleased superiors through harsh exaction were praised as effective.

sentences.zh: 是使為令者惴惴惟財賦是念，朝不謀夕，亦何暇為陛下奉行寬恤詔書、承流宣化者哉？

translations.literal: This makes magistrates anxious only about revenue, planning no further than the day, with no leisure to carry out Your Majesty's leniency edicts or spread transforming influence.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates thus lived in fear for revenue alone, with no time to enforce Your Majesty's relief edicts or carry out benevolent governance.

sentences.zh: 」吏部侍郎許興古議：「今銓曹有知縣、令二百餘闕，無願就者，正緣財賦督迫被罪，所以畏避如此。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. Vice Minister of Personnel Xu Xinggu deliberated: "The appointments office now has over two hundred vacant posts for prefectural prefects and county magistrates; none wish to take them, precisely because revenue pressure leads to punishment—hence such dread and avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Xu Xinggu replied: "More than two hundred county and prefectural posts now stand vacant because officials fear punishment for failing to meet revenue targets.

sentences.zh: 若罷獻羨餘，蠲民積欠，謹擇守臣，戒飭監司，則吏稱民安矣。

translations.literal: If presentation of surplus revenues is abolished, accumulated people's arrears remitted, frontier officials carefully chosen, and intendants admonished, then officials would be praised and the people secure.
translations.idiomatic: If surplus-revenue tributes were abolished, accumulated arrears forgiven, local chiefs carefully chosen, and intendants warned to enforce relief, officials and people alike would be at ease.

sentences.zh: 」乃詔行之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. Thereupon an edict ordered implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered these measures carried out.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，上聞江西盜賊，謂輔臣曰：「輕徭薄賦，所以息盜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the emperor heard of Jiangxi bandits and said to chief ministers: "Light corvée and reduced taxes are how banditry is quelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, hearing of banditry in Jiangxi, the emperor told his chief ministers: "Light corvée and low taxes are what keep people from turning to banditry.

sentences.zh: 歲之水旱，所不能免，儻不寬恤而惟務科督，豈使民不為盜之意哉？

translations.literal: Annual flood and drought cannot be avoided; if there is no leniency and only collection and compulsion, is that the intent of keeping people from becoming bandits?
translations.idiomatic: Floods and droughts come every year and cannot be prevented. If we refuse relief and only press collection, is that how we keep people from becoming bandits?

sentences.zh: 」於是詔諸路州縣，紹興二十七年以前積欠官錢三百九十七萬餘緡及四等以下官欠，悉除之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation. Thereupon an edict to all circuits' prefectures and counties remitted accumulated government debts before the twenty-seventh year of Shaoxing of over 3.97 million strings and official debts of fourth rank and below.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered all circuits to remit more than 3.97 million strings in accumulated public debts before Shaoxing 27, along with debts owed by officials of fourth rank and below.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔：兩浙、江東西水，浙東、江東西螟，其租稅盡蠲之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, an edict: for flooding in Two-Zhe and Jiang East and West, and leaf-borers in Zhe East and Jiang East and West, rent and tax were all remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict remitted all rent and tax in Two Zhe and Jiang East and West after flooding, and in Zhe East and Jiang East and West after crop damage from leaf-borers.

sentences.zh: 自是水旱、經兵，時有蠲減，不盡書也。

translations.literal: From this, flood, drought, and military distress occasioned remissions and reductions from time to time—not all recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter flood, drought, and war brought periodic remissions and reductions, not all of which are recorded here.

sentences.zh: 三十二年六月戊寅，孝宗受禪赦：「凡官司債負、房賃、租賦、和買、役錢及坊場、河渡等錢，自紹興三十年以前並除之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the wuyin day of the thirty-second year, Xiaozong's accession amnesty: "All government debts, house rents, rent and tribute, equitable purchase, corvée cash, and workshop, ferry, and similar fees before the thirtieth year of Shaoxing are all remitted.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day in the sixth month of the thirty-second year, Xiaozong's accession amnesty declared: "All government debts, house rents, land tax, equitable purchase, corvée fees, and workshop, ferry, and similar charges owed before Shaoxing 30 are remitted.

sentences.zh: 諸路或假貢奉為名，漁奪民利，使所在居民以土物為苦，太上皇帝已嘗降詔禁約。

translations.literal: Some circuits under the name of tribute preyed on the people's profit, making local residents suffer from local products; the Retired Emperor had already issued edicts forbidding this.
translations.idiomatic: Some circuits had preyed on the people in the name of tribute, burdening locals with local products. The Retired Emperor had already forbidden this.

sentences.zh: 自今州軍條上土貢之物，當議參酌天地、祖宗陵寢薦獻及德壽宮甘旨之奉，止許長吏修貢，其餘並罷。

translations.literal: From now let prefectures and armies list tribute items, deliberating with reference to offerings at the altars of Heaven and Earth, ancestral tombs, and delicacies for De Shou Palace—only chief local officials may present tribute; all else is abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth prefectures and garrisons were to list tribute items only for offerings at the altars of Heaven and Earth, ancestral tombs, and delicacies for De Shou Palace; only chief local officials might present them, and all other tribute was abolished.

sentences.zh: 州縣因緣多取，以違制坐之。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties who on this pretext take more shall be punished for violation of regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties that took more on this pretext would be punished for violating regulations.

sentences.zh: 」七月，諸縣受民已輸稅租等鈔，不即銷簿者，當職官吏並科罪；

translations.literal: Closing quotation. In the seventh month, where counties received tax and rent chao already paid by the people but did not promptly cancel the ledger, responsible officials were all punished;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month officials in counties that accepted tax and rent receipts without promptly canceling the register were punished;

sentences.zh: 民齎戶鈔不為使，而抑令重輸者，以違制論，不以赦免，著為令。

translations.literal: where people bearing household chao found them not accepted and were forced to pay again, it was treated as violation of regulations, not exempted by amnesty, and codified as statute.
translations.idiomatic: and officials who refused valid household chao and forced taxpayers to pay again were charged with violating regulations, without amnesty, and the rule was written into law.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔：「州縣受納秋苗，官吏多收加耗，肆為奸欺。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, an edict: "When prefectures and counties receive autumn seed-tax, officials often collect extra surcharges and commit fraud at will.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict declared: "When prefectures and counties collect autumn grain tax, officials often take illegal surcharges and commit fraud.

sentences.zh: 方時艱虞，用度未足，欲減常賦而未能，豈忍使貪贓之徒重為民蠹？

translations.literal: At this time of difficulty, expenses are insufficient; though we wish to reduce regular levies and cannot, how can we bear to let greedy corrupt men again be pests to the people?
translations.idiomatic: These are hard times and revenues are short; though we cannot yet cut regular levies, how can we tolerate corrupt officials preying on the people again?

sentences.zh: 自今違犯官吏，並置重典，仍沒其家。」

translations.literal: From now violators among officials shall all receive heavy punishment, and their property confiscated." Closing quotation.
translations.idiomatic: From now on offending officials will face severe punishment and confiscation of property."

translations.idiomatic: Arrears owed by the top three household ranks and influential families were not remitted even by amnesty.
